notes: Found by the 2026-07-10 end-to-end reporting audit (farm-expert FARM-HIGH-003 + data-expert DATA-HIGH-003, corroborated). Fix: SUM((hp.estimates->>'estimatedBiomass')::numeric) and GROUP BY/ORDER BY COALESCE(s."officialCode", s.code), weekday.

title: Disease varsling assembler regression: the FARM-HIGH-203 batch-scoped EXISTS used tb."batchId" = he."batchId" but tank_batches has no batchId column (real: primaryBatchId + batchDetails jsonb), so DISEASE_OUTBREAK prefill still threw 42703; it also did not exclude resolved/cancelled outbreaks, offering a closed event for a legally-immediate varsling
rule_violated: The site scope must use the real tank_batches columns (primaryBatchId + batchDetails jsonb, mirroring BiomassReportAssembler.queryStockings); the SQL-pinning spec locked the wrong column in — a real-DB integration test is the durable guard (FARM-MEDIUM-212).
notes: Regression in the FARM-HIGH-203 fix, caught by the 2026-07-10 audit (data-expert DATA-HIGH-002 + farm-expert FARM-MEDIUM-008). Fix: primaryBatchId + batchDetails jsonb EXISTS pattern; add he.status NOT IN ('resolved','cancelled'); spec now pins the real columns.

title: ReportSchedulerService acquired pg_try_advisory_lock and released pg_advisory_unlock through separate dataSource.query() calls (different pooled connections), so the session lock leaked onto the acquiring connection and was never released; every later run of all four regulatory crons then self-skipped, silently halting rollover, deadline sweep and retry replay for all tenants
rule_violated: A session-scoped advisory lock must be acquired and released on the same connection; DataSource.query() borrows an arbitrary pooled connection per call. Root-cause: hold one dedicated QueryRunner for the lock lifetime.
notes: Triple-confirmed by the 2026-07-10 audit (circuit-breaker CIRCUIT-HIGH-001, multi-tenant REG-HIGH-001, job-queue PRODUCT-JOB-CRITICAL-001). Fixed: runJob holds one dedicated QueryRunner, acquire + release provably the same session, released in finally + runner released after. Tier-3 guard: spec asserts acquire/release share one connection and release-on-throw.

title: FeedingCronService has the same advisory-lock-on-pooled-connection defect as ReportSchedulerService: tryAcquireAdvisoryLock and releaseAdvisoryLock both run through dataSource.query() (different pooled connections) across four cron methods, so the feeding-automation session lock leaks and every later feeding cron run self-skips
rule_violated: Same root cause as FARM-CRITICAL-161; the fix must be applied consistently across every advisory-lock user (no one-off patch to a single service).
notes: Found while fixing FARM-CRITICAL-161. Same mechanical fix: hold one dedicated QueryRunner per job for lock+work+unlock. HIGH (not CRITICAL) only because feeding cron degradation is operationally less immediate than a missed statutory regulatory deadline; still a silent cron-halt.

title: A report draft and its regulatory_reports submission row were two unlinked state machines: a draft was marked SUBMITTED only on synchronous first-call success, so a retry-sweep success or a PERMANENT failure left it READY, and autoSubmitForTenant re-listed and re-filed it every rollover — duplicating an already-accepted Mattilsynet filing (receipt nulled) or infinitely re-sending a rejected one
rule_violated: The regulatory_reports row (klientReferanse = draft.id) is the SSoT for a draft's submission; approveAndSubmit must reconcile the draft from it and be idempotent, never re-filing an accepted report.
notes: Fixed: approveAndSubmit looks up the report by klientReferanse; an accepted (SUBMITTED/QUEUED) row reconciles the draft to its receipt and returns without re-POST; an automated (AUTO_SUBMIT_ACTOR_ID) re-file over a non-accepted row is refused (retry sweep owns transient, operator owns permanent); an explicit operator re-approval may still retry.

title: RegulatoryReportStoreService.upsert unconditionally reset an existing row to PENDING and nulled its Mattilsynet receipt with no terminal-state guard, so any re-entry for an already-accepted klientReferanse silently converted an authoritative SUBMITTED/QUEUED filing into a PENDING row with no receipt — the local record-of-submission lied about a filing that succeeded
rule_violated: An accepted regulatory filing is immutable; a re-entry for an accepted klientReferanse must be an idempotent no-op, a genuine correction files under a new klientReferanse.
notes: Fixed at the persistence layer as defense-in-depth to the FARM-CRITICAL-163 reconciliation: upsert returns a SUBMITTED/QUEUED row unchanged (logs a warning) instead of resetting it. A DB-level UPDATE/DELETE immutability trigger on accepted regulatory_reports rows (mirroring farm_audit_logs) remains a follow-up hardening.

title: farm-module regulatory hooks use hand-written GraphQL types instead of codegen, so enum-casing / field-shape drift from the SDL (root cause of FARM-CRITICAL-165) is only caught by review, not the compiler; the aquamobil client is already codegen-backed and the farm-graphql-fe-be-parity invariant checks only root operation names, not sub-fields or enum casing
rule_violated: Make it impossible (tier 1): FE types must be generated from the schema so casing/shape drift is a compile error, as aquamobil already does.
notes: Tier-1 durable fix for the FARM-CRITICAL-165 class. Migrate farm-module to graphql-codegen (Phase 8.4) and/or extend farm-graphql-fe-be-parity to validate selected sub-fields + enum value casing. Larger workstream; the interim guard is the enum-casing unit tests landed with FARM-CRITICAL-165.

title: Enum-casing drift killed two report flows: farm-module sent lowercase enum VALUES (welfare_impact/high/suspected) while the GraphQL SDL exposes the uppercase KEYS, so the welfare + disease varsling failed enum coercion; and ReportsDueSection compared draft status === 'ready' when the wire is 'READY', so Approve & Submit never rendered for any scheduled draft
rule_violated: Frontend GraphQL enum values must match the SDL wire names; the durable SSoT is codegen-generated types (FARM-MEDIUM-166).
notes: Fixed: welfare/disease varsling inputs retyped to the uppercase wire unions with domain->wire maps at the tab boundary; ReportDraftStatusValue + ReportsDueSection comparisons uppercased. A vitest guard asserts the mutation sends WELFARE_IMPACT/HIGH/CONFIRMED, and the ReportsDueSection spec fixtures now use the real uppercase wire status (both were false-greens on lowercase).

title: buildWirePayload spread the flat assembled slakt body verbatim, but the official slakt schemas require the species arrays nested in utførteLokaliteter/planlagteLokaliteter (additionalProperties:false), so every scheduled slaughter draft failed official-schema validation and could never be submitted
rule_violated: The draft→wire transform must produce the exact official wire shape; a flat body that cannot pass additionalProperties:false is a dead submission path.
notes: Fixed: reshapeForWire wraps the executed arter into utførteLokaliteter and the planned ukeplanPerArt into planlagteLokaliteter (one locality = the draft's site, carrying the header org/lokalitet), dropping the assembler-only totalKgPerArt. Specs assert the nested wrapper + no top-level leak. Corroborated by farm-expert FARM-HIGH-002 + contract CONTRACT-HIGH-003.

title: The manual executed-slaughter wizard filed a fabricated government report: it placed the quality-grade PERCENTAGES straight into the Mattilsynet superiorKg/ordinaerKg/produksjonsfiskKg/utkastKg weight fields and hard-coded art='SAL', so e.g. 50 000 kg of 80% Superior trout was filed as 80 kg of salmon — structurally schema-valid but fully falsified
rule_violated: No fabricated value may reach a regulator; executed slaughter must be filed from harvest records (per-species gutted kg) via the records-based review-and-approve draft, not a percentage form that has no species breakdown.
notes: Fixed by making the fabrication impossible: useSubmitExecutedSlaughterReport is no longer imported by the tab, the executed submit fails closed with guidance to the records-based draft, and the Executed Slaughter selector is a disabled affordance pointing to Scheduled reports due (now submittable per FARM-HIGH-167). Follow-up: the now-unreachable 'completed' wizard steps are dead code to be removed with the FARM-MEDIUM-009 parallel-systems cleanup. Planned-slaughter species/dedup residual (FARM-LOW-014) tracked separately.

title: Migration 1804400 dropped harvest_records.qualityGrade from every tenant schema during the source-first farm pass, but a tenant not yet migrated to the expand migration 1803100 (which backfills qualityClass FROM qualityGrade) then hit 42703 when its tenant pass ran, aborting the whole deploy on any DB with pre-existing tenant schemas (first prod deploy or replay onto a snapshot)
rule_violated: A source-first per-schema fan-out cannot drop a column another schema's not-yet-run expand migration still reads; the drop must be each schema's own ordered pass, never a cross-schema sweep in the source pass.
notes: Fixed: removed the aggressive cross-schema DROP COLUMN loop (each schema's own 1804300 drops qualityGrade after its 1803100 backfill), and the type-reclamation now DEFERS (returns) when any schema still references the shared type instead of masking-then-dropping. bootstrap-from-scratch missed it (empty DB → zero tenant schemas).

title: The shared farm.harvest_records_qualitygrade_enum type is left orphaned after FARM-CRITICAL-169: because 1804300 and 1804400 ship in the same release, 1804400's farm pass always sees tenant columns still referencing the type and defers the DROP TYPE, and it never re-runs — so the orphan type is reclaimed only by a post-fan-out step in a later release
rule_violated: A shared object whose dependents span tenant schemas must be reclaimed by a step that runs AFTER all tenant passes complete, not by a source-pass migration that runs before them.
notes: Follow-up to FARM-CRITICAL-169. Clean durable fix (data-expert option b): a post-fan-out reclamation hook in apps/db-migrate/src/main.ts that DROPs the orphan enum after every tenant pass has run 1804300. The deferred orphan type is harmless (no active dependents once all tenants catch up).

title: The three regulatory external calls (Maskinporten discovery, Maskinporten token, Mattilsynet submit) were raw fetch() with no circuit breaker and no timeout, despite a CI-mandated canonical CircuitBreakerService; a hung or slow government API had zero backpressure and no bounded wait, and under the serial lock-held sweep one slow downstream stalled the whole cron and every tenant
rule_violated: Every external-dependency call must have a bounded timeout and a per-tenant fail-closed circuit breaker (the canonical CircuitBreakerService), so one tenant's failing government integration cannot hang threads or cascade to others.
notes: Fixed: AbortSignal.timeout on all three fetches (5s auth, 20s submit); CircuitBreakerModule registered in RegulatoryModule; Maskinporten discovery wrapped (global key) + token wrapped (per-tenant), both fail-closed and throwing on failure so the breaker counts them; Mattilsynet submit wrapped per-tenant fail-closed (counts network/timeout + slow-call; on open → CircuitOpenError → caught → transient replay, never a fabricated acceptance).

title: Regulatory resilience refinements remain: retry backoff has no jitter (synchronized retry herd), Maskinporten token has no single-flight dedup (thundering herd on cache expiry), the token cache is FIFO-evicted at 100 (re-auth thrash past ~20 tenants), and the submit breaker counts network/timeout/slow but not 5xx
rule_violated: Retry storms and thundering herds against a struggling government API/auth server must be damped (jitter + single-flight + LRU); a breaker should count HTTP failures, not only transport failures.
notes: Follow-ups to FARM-CRITICAL-171 (CIRCUIT-MEDIUM-001/002/003 + the 5xx-in-breaker refinement). Add full jitter to computeNextAttempt; memoize the in-flight token promise per cacheKey; make the token cache LRU sized to the tenant population; have the submit breaker fn throw on 5xx/timeout (not on a 4xx validation rejection) so HTTP failures trip it.

title: The direct REST submit mutations took organisasjonsnummer + lokalitetsnummer straight from the GraphQL client and never verified them against the tenant's configured sites/org (the draft path derives them server-side), so a MODULE_MANAGER could file a legally-binding Mattilsynet report attributing it to any org/lokalitet the tenant credential could reach, not a real tenant-owned site
rule_violated: Client-declared regulatory identity on a government submission must be verified server-side against the tenant's configured sites (fail-closed), never trusted from the request.
notes: Fixed: assertTenantOwnsIdentity verifies every declared (org, lokalitet) pair against getEffectiveSiteLocalityMappings + getEffectiveOrganisationNumber, called at the top of all five REST submit mutations (top-level + nested slakt localities). Rejects a foreign lokalitet or mismatched org with BadRequestException before any persistence/submission. Specs assert both rejection paths.

title: The daily deadline sweep and the reportDeadlines view loaded EVERY draft ever created for the tenant (repo.find on tenantId only) then discarded terminal/undated rows in JS, so both scans grew unbounded with history — years of SUBMITTED/DISMISSED drafts re-read and thrown away every day
rule_violated: Filter predicates belong in SQL, not a post-load JS pass; an unbounded per-tick full-table scan is a scale trap.
notes: Fixed: new listDeadlineCandidates pushes status NOT IN (SUBMITTED,DISMISSED) AND dueAt IS NOT NULL into SQL (the (tenantId,status) index covers it); listDeadlines and the scheduler's notifyDeadlinesForTenant both use it. Specs assert the SQL where and the sweep no longer JS-filters terminal rows.

title: The submission retry pipeline had no max-attempt / dead-letter: a chronically-failing TRANSIENT report (a persistent 403 auth misconfig, or a multi-day outage) rescheduled every 6h indefinitely, and the operator-notification event fires only on PERMANENT, so a functionally-stuck report was never surfaced and silently missed its deadline
rule_violated: A retry policy must terminate: on exhaustion the work is dead-lettered and surfaced, never retried forever.
notes: Fixed: MAX_TRANSIENT_ATTEMPTS=12 ceiling; on exhaustion the TRANSIENT path escalates through the extracted markPermanentFailure (terminal PERMANENT + the same operator-notification outbox event) so the retry sweep stops replaying it and the failure surfaces. Spec asserts dead-letter escalation at attempt 12 (no reschedule, applyFailure PERMANENT, one outbox event).

title: The scheduler assembled a BIOMASS draft into regulatory_report_drafts every month, which surfaced in Scheduled reports due with a Mattilsynet Approve & Submit that always threw (BIOMASS is not a REST report), and duplicated the biomass_reports FD-0001/Altinn state machine — a false-channel affordance plus a no-duplicate-structures violation
rule_violated: Biomass is the Fiskeridirektoratet FD-0001/Altinn manual channel (biomass_reports SSoT); it must not flow through the Mattilsynet REST draft pipeline (no duplicate structures).
notes: Fixed: BIOMASS removed from monthlyJobs so no BIOMASS draft is created in the REST pipeline; biomass keeps its own biomass_reports + Altinn READY->CONFIRMED_SUBMITTED flow. Spec asserts monthlyJobs no longer contains BIOMASS.

title: The settefisk assembler's mortality/culls/external_out CTEs filtered only by tenantId + date, not by site, so each aggregated the tenant's ENTIRE mortality_records / tank_operations history and the final query then discarded the non-site rows — and the scheduler runs it once per site, so a 30-site tenant re-scanned the whole-tenant tables 30x per monthly rollover
rule_violated: Aggregation CTEs must be scoped to the query's site tanks so they seek on the (tankId, date) index, not scan the whole-tenant table per site.
notes: Fixed: each CTE joins site_tanks on the source tankId, so the mortality/cull/transfer aggregations use the (tankId, recordDate/operationDate) index for the site's handful of tanks instead of a whole-tenant scan. Spec (mocked query) green.

title: regulatory_report_drafts (the fully-assembled Mattilsynet payloads — the richest per-tenant dataset) shipped without the FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY backstop its sibling regulatory_reports carries, so only search_path + the where:{tenantId} filter protected it against a query that omits the tenantId predicate
rule_violated: Every per-tenant table in an RLS-adopting service must carry FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY as the row-level backstop, not rely on the application query shape alone.
notes: Fixed: migration 1804500000000 applies the same applyTenantRlsToSchema FORCE-RLS policy the reports table has, fanned out to farm + every tenant schema, with a postCondition asserting relforcerowsecurity. The draft service's scoped-repo reads are now RLS-protected regardless of query shape.

title: The GDPR Art 17 tenant-erasure cascade hard-deleted regulatory_reports and biomass_reports along with every other tenant-scoped table, destroying the government-filed Mattilsynet/Fiskeridirektoratet submission records that Norwegian aquaculture law requires be retained under the Art 17(3)(b) legal-obligation carve-out
rule_violated: Records retained under a legal obligation (GDPR Art 17(3)(b)) must survive a right-to-erasure cascade; erasure of the personal data in them is honoured by anonymising the identifying columns in place, not by hard-deleting the legally-required record.
notes: Fixed: a STATUTORY_RETENTION_POLICY SSoT map (regulatory_reports->[submittedBy], biomass_reports->[generatedBy,submittedBy,confirmedBy]) drives the cascade: listed tables are skipped by the DELETE pass and routed through anonymiseRetainedRecords, which hashes the operator-identifying UUID columns in place (same stable SHA-256 prefix as farm_audit_logs). The retention outcome (retainedRowsByTable + retainedRowsAnonymised) is persisted on tenant_erasure_audit and reconstructed on ALREADY_PURGED replay so matchedRecordCount stays byte-identical. Spec: 3 new cases assert the tables are never deleted, are anonymised, zero-match skips the UPDATE, and replay reconstructs the accounting.

title: The regulatory-reporting module wrote no farm_audit_logs row for any regulator action, so a filed Mattilsynet/Fiskeridirektoratet submission and its approval, dismissal, field-override, and failure left no immutable, actor-attributed audit trail (SOC 2 CC4 / GDPR Art 30 accountability gap on the government-submission pipeline)
rule_violated: Every regulated, actor-initiated action (regulator submission, approval, dismissal, override, failure) must write an immutable, actor-attributed audit row, committed atomically with the state change it records.
notes: Fixed: audit wired at the persistence choke points so every path is attributed automatically. Store transitions write REGULATORY_SUBMITTED (markSubmitted accept + recordQueued varsling) and REGULATORY_FAILED (applyFailure) via AuditLogService.logWithManager inside the same tenant transaction, actor = row.submittedBy — covering interactive submit, draft auto-submit, and retry-sweep replay. Draft lifecycle writes REGULATORY_APPROVED (markSubmitted), REGULATORY_DISMISSED (dismissDraft), REGULATORY_OVERRIDDEN (saveOverrides) via repo.manager.transaction with the operator threaded from the resolver. Five new farm_audit_logs_action_enum values (migration 1804700000000, type-presence-guarded fan-out mirroring 1801300000000). Specs assert each action fires with the right actor; farm-service 227 suites/1399 tests green.

title: The biomass assembler stamped the CURRENT live standing stock as a historical month's closing beholdning with RECORDS provenance, so refreshing a report for an old period filed today's inventory as that month-end figure to Fiskeridirektoratet — a truthfulness violation on a regulatory number
rule_violated: A field may only carry RECORDS provenance when the source data actually reflects the reported period; a live 'as of now' figure must not be presented as a historical period-end value.
notes: Fixed (truthfulness): a pure isStandingStockStale(periodEnd, now) helper (calendar-based, DST-safe: fresh iff the period end is in the current or immediately-preceding month) gates the /currentBiomass provenance. For the current/just-closed period the live stock is a fair proxy and stays RECORDS; for a materially historical period the assembler fails closed to a blocking MANUAL_REQUIRED with an actionable message, so auto-submit cannot file a stale number and the operator must supply the real closing beholdning. The deeper architectural fix — a point-in-time stock ledger — is tracked as FARM-HIGH-182. Specs: period.util staleness boundaries (fresh/stale/year-boundary) + assembler flips to blocking MANUAL_REQUIRED for a historical period; farm-service 1405 tests green.

title: farm-service has no point-in-time stock ledger, so a historical month-end standing stock (beholdning) cannot be reconstructed — the biomass calculator only exposes the live mirror, and the stock read-model snapshots are current-state-only, forcing a fail-closed MANUAL_REQUIRED for any biomass report older than last month
rule_violated: Regulatory period-end quantities should be reconstructable from source records for any past period, not only approximated by the current live inventory.
notes: Follow-on to FARM-HIGH-181. A faithful historical beholdning needs point-in-time reconstruction (initial stocking replayed forward through dated mortality_records / tank_operations cull+transfer / harvest_records to the period end, or a snapshot-per-period ledger). Blocked this session on: (1) no live DB in the environment to verify complex reconstruction SQL, and (2) a double-counting hazard between mortality_records and tank_operations.'mortality'/'harvest' operation types that requires establishing which is the mirror's SSoT before replay is safe. Until built, FARM-HIGH-181 fails closed to MANUAL_REQUIRED for stale periods so no false RECORDS number is filed.

title: Both regulatory CSV exporters (backend FD-0001 Altinn export and the frontend submissions export) applied RFC-4180 quoting but no formula-injection neutralisation, so a tenant-controlled species/feed name or a Mattilsynet-echoed feilmelding beginning with = + - @ would execute as a formula when the CSV is opened in Excel/Sheets
rule_violated: Exported CSV cells whose value could be interpreted as a spreadsheet formula must be neutralised (OWASP CSV Injection), not merely RFC-4180 quoted.
notes: Fixed: both csvCell (backend) and csvEscape (frontend) prefix a string cell whose first character is a formula trigger (= + - @ tab CR) with a single quote so it opens as literal text, then apply RFC-4180 quoting. The backend guard skips numeric cells so legitimate negative/formatted numbers stay numeric. Specs assert =cmd/=HYPERLINK payloads and the +,-,@ triggers are neutralised and never emitted as a bare formula; backend 5 + farm-module 167 tests green.

title: Regulator error bodies and thrown errors were logged via raw string interpolation on the Mattilsynet submit and Maskinporten token/discovery paths, so a response echoing the submitted kontaktperson (name/e-mail/phone), org numbers, or OAuth detail reached the log stream unmasked and unbounded — bypassing the platform maskPii discipline
rule_violated: PII and third-party error bodies must be masked (maskPii) and length-bounded before logging; raw error/response interpolation into log messages is banned.
notes: Fixed: every regulator error-body / thrown-error log site now routes the value through maskAndTruncatePii (mask emails/phones/SSN/CC/IPv4 + hard length cap) before it reaches the log stream. Sites: MattilsynetApiService.submitReport (the !response.ok body dump + the catch error), MaskinportenService.requestToken (token-endpoint errorText, masked in both the log AND the thrown message it propagates into) + discovery catch, and RegulatoryResolver.testMaskinportenConnection catch. Verification: maskAndTruncatePii is independently unit-tested in backend-common; farm-service 1407 tests + lint green after the change. No bespoke fetch/circuit-breaker harness was added for these private HTTP paths — disproportionate for a one-line application of an already-tested helper.

title: updateAutoSubmitPolicy accepted an arbitrary reportType string (@IsString only) and wrote it straight into the autoSubmitPolicies jsonb, so a client could set an auto-submit opt-in key for BIOMASS, a varsling type, or any nonsense value — polluting settings and creating a false 'will auto-file' affordance for a type with no auto-submit path
rule_violated: Input that becomes a persisted policy key must be validated against a closed SSoT set at the API boundary and defended again at the service layer; free-form strings must never become jsonb keys.
notes: Fixed: a single AUTO_SUBMITTABLE_REPORT_TYPES SSoT (the five REST draft types — SEA_LICE, CLEANER_FISH, SMOLT, SLAUGHTER_PLANNED, SLAUGHTER_EXECUTED) drives both an @IsIn on UpdateAutoSubmitPolicyInput.reportType (API-boundary rejection via the global ValidationPipe) and a BadRequestException guard in updateAutoSubmitPolicy (defence in depth for any non-resolver caller). BIOMASS/varsling/nonsense are rejected and never pollute the jsonb. GraphQL SDL unchanged (validation-only, field stays String — no codegen/parity impact). Specs: parameterised reject (BIOMASS/WELFARE_EVENT/ESCAPE/DISEASE_OUTBREAK/NONSENSE) + accept (all 5 REST types); 16 tests green.

title: The government-submission pipeline had no RED metrics, no cron heartbeat, and no operator alerts, so a Mattilsynet rejection returned GraphQL-200 and counted as success everywhere, a chronically-failing report was invisible, and a wedged regulatory scheduler (no rollover/retry running) went unnoticed
rule_violated: Every external-facing pipeline (especially a regulatory submission path) must emit RED metrics + a cron heartbeat and carry operator alerts with a runbook_url; a failed submission must never be indistinguishable from success.
notes: Fixed: FarmDomainMetricsService gains farm_regulatory_submission_total{report_type,outcome} (submitted/failed/queued — the RED rate+errors), farm_regulatory_cron_runs_total{job,outcome} and a farm_regulatory_cron_last_run_timestamp_seconds{job} heartbeat gauge — all on the existing private registry, no tenant label per the label discipline. The submission counter is emitted at the store choke points (markSubmitted/applyFailure/recordQueued), so every path (interactive, auto-submit, retry replay, varsling) is covered; the cron metrics are emitted in the scheduler runJob wrapper (success/error/skipped_locked, heartbeat on every run incl. lock-skip so passive replicas don't false-alarm). Three operator alerts added to farm-data-ssot-alerts.yml (FailuresElevated, RetrySweepStalled heartbeat, CronErrored) each with runbook_url. Specs: metrics-service series assertions, store-choke-point outcome assertions, scheduler heartbeat assertions (success/error/skipped); farm-service 1419 + alert-runbook-url invariant green.

title: Slaughter drafts could never be submitted because the assembled body kept arter/ukeplanPerArt (plus the assembler-only totalKgPerArt) at the top level instead of nesting them in the official utførteLokaliteter/planlagteLokaliteter single-locality wrapper, so every slaughter draft failed the additionalProperties:false official schema
rule_violated: The assembled draft body must be reshaped into the exact official wire format before submission; a slaughter draft must validate against the official additionalProperties:false schema.
notes: Fix landed earlier via reshapeForWire (buildWirePayload -> reshapeForWire nests arter into utførteLokaliteter for SLAUGHTER_EXECUTED and ukeplanPerArt into planlagteLokaliteter for SLAUGHTER_PLANNED, drops the assembler-only totalKgPerArt, header spread last). This step VERIFIES + guards it: reshapeForWire is now exported and a new contract test in official-schema-contract.spec.ts feeds a realistic assembled slaughter body through reshapeForWire and validates the output against the REAL official Ajv schema (getOfficialSchemaValidator), asserting valid + zero errors + that arter/ukeplanPerArt/totalKgPerArt are absent from the top level. Previously the draft-submission spec mocked the validator, so nothing proved schema validity; a future assembler/reshape change that re-breaks the wire shape now fails in CI. Top-level key sets confirmed to exactly match the schema required set for both types. 18 contract tests green.

title: A SUBMITTED regulatory report — the legal record of what was filed to Mattilsynet — could be silently overwritten: regulatory-report-store.upsert had no terminal-state guard and there was no DB immutability trigger, so a bug or raw path could reset an accepted row to PENDING and null its receipt
rule_violated: A terminal, government-filed record must be immutable at the strongest available tier (a DB trigger), not only guarded in application code.
notes: Fixed in two tiers. Tier-2/3 (landed earlier): upsert refuses to reset a SUBMITTED/QUEUED row to PENDING and returns it unchanged. Tier-1 (this step, make-it-impossible): migration 1804800000000 installs a BEFORE UPDATE trigger (current_schema-relative, fans out to farm + every tenant schema, table-presence guarded) that RAISEs if a SUBMITTED row's filing-identity fields (status, klientReferanse, reportType, payload, referanse) change; benign updatedAt writes and the transition INTO SUBMITTED are allowed. QUEUED is deliberately excluded (recordQueued inserts-then-sets-referanse; QUEUED stays on the service guard). Verification: migration-sql-lint + the migration postCondition (installation, runs in CI migration-harness) + the existing upsert-immutability service spec + a new .postgres.spec.ts exercising the trigger behavior against real Postgres (reject status/referanse/payload change on SUBMITTED, allow updatedAt-only, allow PENDING->SUBMITTED, allow QUEUED update). The postgres spec runs in CI (Docker/testcontainers), not in this sandbox.

title: The biomass assembler defaulted a stocking row with no recorded avg weight to 0 kg and tagged the /stockings section RECORDS, so an unknown-weight stocking was filed to Fiskeridirektoratet as a truthful zero-biomass record
rule_violated: A value derived from a missing source field must not be presented as RECORDS; unknown is not zero.
notes: Fixed: the assembler tracks stocking batches whose avgWeightG is null and, when any exist, flags /stockings as MANUAL_REQUIRED (non-blocking) naming the affected batch(es) instead of fromRecords — the row is still emitted with a 0 placeholder but its provenance tells the truth. Spec asserts the flip. farm-service green.

title: The AES-256-GCM encrypted-column transformer's insecure dev-only fallback key was gated only on NODE_ENV !== 'production', so staging, an unset NODE_ENV in CI, or any typo'd env value silently encrypted real Maskinporten secrets and PII with the public 'dddd…' key
rule_violated: An insecure dev fallback must be opt-in from a known development environment, not the default for every non-production environment; secret material must fail closed.
notes: Fixed platform-wide in the single SSoT resolveKey (createEncryptedColumnTransformer, used by farm regulatory + worker PII, HR employee PII, AI config, sentinel-hub): the dev fallback now requires NODE_ENV explicitly 'development' or 'test'; production, staging, unset, and any other value throw when no key is set. Jest sets NODE_ENV=test so all specs keep the fallback. New spec asserts fallback on test/development, fail-closed on production/staging/unset, and explicit-key works regardless of NODE_ENV (6 tests). backend-common encryption suite green (14).

title: welfare_assessments and lice_counts had no DB CHECK constraints, so a welfare score outside 0-3 or a negative lice stage count (from a capture bug or raw write) could be stored and flow into a Mattilsynet report
rule_violated: Domain range invariants (welfare 0-3, lice non-negative, positive sample size) belong in the database as CHECK constraints, not only in application validation.
notes: Fixed: migration 1804900000000 adds CHECK constraints (current_schema-relative fan-out, table-presence + duplicate_object guarded): welfare gill/fin/wound/deformity scores BETWEEN 0 AND 3, lice adultFemale/mobile/attached >= 0, and fishSampled > 0 on both tables. postCondition asserts the constraints exist where the tables do. migration-sql-lint + array-completeness green.

title: applyFailure incremented regulatory_reports.attemptCount with an unlocked read-modify-write, so an operator resubmit racing the retry sweep could both read attemptCount=N and write N+1 — a lost increment plus a clobbered nextAttemptAt/status on the same filing row
rule_violated: A read-modify-write on a shared row that concurrent workers touch must serialise (row lock or atomic UPDATE), not race.
notes: Fixed: applyFailure and markSubmitted now take a pessimistic_write row lock (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) on the findOneOrFail, so a concurrent failure/success on the same row serialises and the second reads the committed attemptCount. Both always run inside a transaction (recordFailure's runInTenantTransaction / markSubmitted's, or the caller's for the PERMANENT+outbox path). Specs assert the lock option is passed. farm-service green.

title: Manual draft overrides arriving as JSON strings (e.g. sjøtemperatur '12.5') failed the official Ajv schema, which declares those fields as numbers, so an operator filling a blocking MANUAL_REQUIRED numeric field with a string got a hard validation rejection instead of a submittable draft
rule_violated: Form-derived scalar values should be coerced to the schema's declared type before validation; a numeric-string override must not fail a numeric field.
notes: Fixed: the official schema Ajv instance now uses coerceTypes:true — schema-directed scalar coercion (a numeric-string like '12.5' for a number field becomes 12.5; a non-numeric string still fails). It does NOT relax required/additionalProperties:false/enum/format, so the trust-boundary gate stays strict. Ajv coerces in place and the validator returns that same object, so the wire payload carries the correct types; correctly-typed interactive DTOs are a no-op. Specs: numeric-string coerces + validates, non-numeric string still throws; contract suite (18) + reshape guard green.

title: The regulatory assemblers forked their own artskode validation regex — escape used /^[A-Z]{3}$/ while settefisk used the looser /^[A-Z]{2,5}$/, so settefisk would pass a 2- or 5-character non-official species code straight to Mattilsynet
rule_violated: A validation shape used across modules must have one SSoT, not per-assembler forks that drift.
notes: Fixed (closes FARM-MEDIUM-213 / FARM-LOW-011): a single OFFICIAL_ARTSKODE_PATTERN = /^[A-Z]{3}$/ SSoT is exported from official-species-codes.ts (every official code in the seed map is exactly 3 uppercase letters), and both the escape and settefisk assemblers import it instead of forking. The loose {2,5} settefisk fork is removed. Assembler specs green.

title: The regulatory assemblers that read more than one table opened a separate runInTenantRead per sub-query (lakselus lice+treatments, rensefisk composition+ledger, biomass stockings+slaughter), so each sub-query paid the full connect->pin->assert->commit->release tenant-boundary round-trip, multiplied per site per rollover
rule_violated: Multiple reads for one assemble should share a single tenant-read boundary, not open a fresh boundary (connect/pin/assert/commit/release) per query.
notes: Fixed: the three multi-read assemblers now run all their direct DB reads inside ONE runInTenantRead boundary (query methods take the shared QueryRunner and call qr.query), collapsing 2 boundaries to 1 each. Separate services (WaterTemperatureService, BiomassCalculatorService) and CQRS queries own their own boundaries and still run in parallel with the consolidated one. The single-read assemblers (disease/escape/welfare/settefisk/slakt) already opened one boundary. Assembler specs are boundary-transparent (key on SQL) and stay green (lakselus 6, rensefisk 3, biomass 5, report-assembly 4).

title: The farm-module remote imported every page-level route eagerly in Module.tsx, so the heavy 8-tab regulatory reporting UI (plus every other page) shipped in one bundle with no code-splitting and no bundle budget — a large initial download for any farm-module user
rule_violated: Page-level routes in a federated remote must be code-split so a heavy feature (regulatory reporting) is not shipped eagerly to every user; the bundle should carry an explicit size budget.
notes: Fixed: every page-level route in Module.tsx is now React.lazy code-split (mirroring the existing BatchDetailPage tab pattern) behind one Suspense boundary with a light fallback, so each route (the regulatory reporting UI in particular) becomes its own async chunk fetched on navigation instead of shipping eagerly. vite build gains an explicit chunkSizeWarningLimit=600kB budget so a regression that re-bundles a heavy page eagerly warns in CI. All page components are default exports (lazy-compatible). farm-module 167 tests + lint + type-check green.

title: The regulatory scheduler's tenant discovery selected the tenantId from the sites table only, so a provisioned tenant schema with regulatory settings but no sites row (e.g. before sites are added, or after all sites were removed) was silently skipped and its deadline/retry sweeps never ran
rule_violated: Tenant discovery for a cron must anchor on a source that reflects the work's SSoT, not one incidental feature table that may be empty.
notes: Fixed: discoverTenantIds now anchors on regulatory_settings (the SSoT for a reporting-configured tenant, populated at setup) UNION sites, so a tenant with settings but no sites row (or vice-versa) is still discovered and its sweeps run. A schema is one tenant so LIMIT 1 on the union still yields that tenant's id. Scheduler spec (19) green.

title: Harvest cancel/update leaves the tank_operations('harvest') mirror un-reversed: delete-harvest-record cancels harvest_records and reverses live stock but never compensates the paired tank_operations('harvest') row, and update-harvest-record edits quantityHarvested without adjusting the mirror — so that ledger over-counts removals for any cancelled/edited harvest.
rule_violated: A double-written mirror ledger must be kept consistent on EVERY state change of the record it mirrors — a cancel/edit that reverses one ledger must reverse the other (or the mirror must be dropped as an SSoT).
notes: Surfaced by the FARM-HIGH-182 SSoT-mapping investigation. FARM-HIGH-182's read-side replay is SAFE because it sources harvest from harvest_records filtered status<>cancelled (not the tank_operations mirror), and the assembler's querySlaughter was fixed to the same filter in the FARM-HIGH-182 commit. The remaining write-path divergence is tracked here: either (a) delete/update-harvest handlers must reverse/adjust the tank_operations('harvest') row in the same transaction, or (b) tank_operations('harvest') is demoted from an SSoT and every consumer sources harvest from harvest_records. Routes to farm-expert (write path) with data-expert consult for any event-contract/migration implications.

title: StockReconstructionService (FARM-HIGH-182) latest_meas used DISTINCT ON (batchId) ORDER BY measurementDate DESC with no tiebreaker; measurementDate is day-granular, so two same-day samplings tie and Postgres returns an arbitrary one — a non-reproducible historical biomass figure (differs across replicas / after VACUUM) and a potentially flaky CI spec.
rule_violated: A regulatory figure reconstructed from source records must be deterministic — a DISTINCT ON / latest-row pick over a day-granular column needs a full tiebreaker (createdAt, id).
notes: Raised by the data-expert re-review of the FARM-HIGH-182 reconstruction. Fixed in the same pass: ORDER BY now appends createdAt DESC, id DESC so the picked measurement (and thus reported biomass) is reproducible.

title: StockReconstructionService's first draft attributed a batch's GLOBAL count to every site it ever touched via an ever-touched membership union, so a batch transferred from site A to B was counted in full at BOTH sites, and the stale-period biomass assembler stamped that inflated number RECORDS (auto-fileable) instead of failing closed — a wrong regulatory beholdning for multi-site salmon tenants.
rule_violated: A per-site regulatory quantity must be attributed to the tank the fish are in at the period end (via signed transfer legs), not a batch-global count behind ever-touched site membership.
notes: Caught by the farm-expert pre-merge re-review of FARM-HIGH-182 (never merged to main; existed in branch commit 3cb16eb4). FIXED: the reconstruction is rewritten to a per-(site tank, batch) point-in-time replay — inflows from signed tank_allocations, removals per-tank from each event's SSoT — so a transferred batch nets to zero at its origin and appears only at its destination, counted once. CI postgres spec asserts the cross-site case.

title: StockReconstructionService's first draft pulled cleaner-fish batches (batchType=CLEANER_FISH) into the FD-0001 production standing stock via an unfiltered operations-membership branch, inflating a salmon site's production beholdning with cleaner-fish stock reported under a different species — the live path excludes cleaner batches entirely.
rule_violated: A production biomass report must include only production batches; cleaner-fish stock is a separate concern and must be excluded, matching the live standing-stock path.
notes: Caught by the farm-expert pre-merge re-review of FARM-HIGH-182 (never merged to main; existed in branch commit 3cb16eb4). FIXED: the rewritten per-tank replay sources inflows from production tank_allocations and removals from production mortality|cull|harvest ledgers (cleaner uses cleaner_* ops / cleanerFishDetails), plus an explicit batchType='production' join filter. CI postgres spec asserts a cleaner batch with production-shaped ledger rows is still excluded.

title: StockReconstructionService could silently omit a pre-FARM-HIGH-112 production batch that is currently resident in a site tank, stocked before T, but carries zero tank_allocations AND zero mortality/cull/harvest at ≤ T — it never enters the replay's pairs, so a site whose only stock is such a batch reconstructs complete=true totalKg=0 and files a wrong '0 kg' RECORDS instead of failing closed.
rule_violated: A reconstruction that can silently omit a resident batch must surface it and fail closed, never report a fabricated zero as RECORDS.
notes: Raised by the farm-expert confirmation re-review of the FARM-HIGH-182 rewrite (pre-merge). FIXED: a `resident` CTE surfaces production batches currently resident in a site tank, stocked ≤ T, with NO tank_allocations, into `pairs` so they hit the existing inflowRows=0 guard and fail the whole site closed. A batch that arrived after T has a transfer_in allocation and is excluded. CI postgres spec asserts the silent-omission case fails closed.

title: batch.service.ts carries a legacy allocateBatchToTank/transferBatch whose transfer path mutates tank_allocations in place (running-balance: sourceAllocation.quantity -= quantity, soft-delete at 0) — incompatible with the signed-immutable-leg model the stock reconstruction relies on. Currently dead (only test-referenced; live mutations dispatch via CommandBus), a latent trap if re-wired.
rule_violated: Dead code that contradicts the current SSoT model (signed immutable allocation legs) must be removed, not left as a latent trap.
notes: Raised by the farm-expert confirmation re-review. Tracked (not fixed in this reporting PR): the methods are dead and only test-referenced, so deleting them + their tests is tangential batch-domain hygiene better kept out of the regulatory-reporting diff. Does not affect the reconstruction (live transfers go via TransferBatchCommand/allocate-to-tank CQRS handlers, which write signed immutable legs).

title: tenant fan-out + provisioner create per-tenant tables owner=superuser with empty ACL — owning service dies with permission-denied at first query (live 2026-07-06 mobile batchMetrics outage); fixed with MODULE_SCHEMAS-derived privilege assertion + deploy-blocking verify at 3 chokepoints
rule_violated: Every per-tenant table carries its schema-owner ownership + service-role DML regardless of creating connection; privilege drift is deploy-blocking, never silent
notes: Adversarially verified (multi-agent audit). Manual prod repair 2026-07-02 for 5 tables; mechanism fix self-heals rest incl. future tables.

title: orphan tenant tables with no owning module (deploy_artifacts, release_bundles) — surfaced by unknownTables warning; register or drop
rule_violated: Every tenant-schema table has a registered owning module
notes: Owner infra-expert, deadline 2026-07-20.

title: AquaMobil has zero regulatory field-capture or report surface (RPT-019 / Phase 6): lice counts, welfare scores and escape incidents cannot be recorded from the field where they happen, and report drafts due cannot be reviewed/approved from mobile — the operational entities the Mattilsynet assemblers read stay desktop-only, so field observations reach the system late or never.
rule_violated: Operational capture must be available at the point of observation (offline-first mobile) or the regulatory source tables under-report; RPT-019.
notes: Phase 6 umbrella finding: offline-first capture pages (lice/welfare/escape) writing the Phase-2 entities with clientCommandId at-most-once receipts, escape priority-drain + immediate-varsling banner, and the online-only reports-due/review-approve surface.

title: tenant-admin MobileSettings.tsx toggle UI drifted from the MobileAllowedFeatures SSoT: it renders/saves only 6 of 12+ flags (transfer/schedule/attendance/leave/tasks/storage and Phase-6 additions are not admin-toggleable) and its local defaults contradict DEFAULT_MOBILE_FEATURES.
rule_violated: Feature-flag vocabulary must be single-sourced; a hand-copied subset in the admin UI silently strips admin control over newer features and seeds wrong defaults.
notes: Pre-existing drift observed while implementing Phase 6 (FARM-HIGH-214). Root-cause fix: derive the toggle list + defaults from a shared vocabulary (codegen from the auth GraphQL MobileAllowedFeatures type or an exported const), not a hand-maintained copy. Not fixed in the Phase-6 slice to keep the diff regulatory-scoped.

title: Mixed-batch containers had no deterministic primary batch on the mobile read path: the farm-stock projection wrote isPrimary=false for ALL detail rows and the inventory handler ordered batchNumber-only, so the mobile mapper's batches[0] species/batch attribution for field capture was alphabetical, not the ledger's primaryBatchId.
rule_violated: Primary-batch attribution must come from the tank-composition ledger's primaryBatchId SSoT, never from incidental ordering.
notes: Raised by farm-expert pre-merge re-review of Phase 6 (FARM-HIGH-214). Fixed in-branch: projection derives isPrimary from primaryBatchId per detail row; handler orders isPrimary DESC first; mobile mapper prefers the explicit isPrimary row.

title: AquaMobil carried a dead GetTanksWithBatches GraphQL document with zero importers that silently desynced from the Tank type's newer fields (siteId/species) — a stale-contract trap for the next reader; the live tank source is farmStockInventory in useTanks.
rule_violated: Dead GraphQL documents are deleted, not left to drift — the codegen gate validates them against the schema but nothing keeps them aligned with the consuming types.
notes: Raised by farm-expert pre-merge re-review of Phase 6 (FARM-HIGH-214). Fixed in-branch: document + unused generated-type imports deleted.

title: Unified SCADA editor HMI palette is a strict, drifted subset of the builder palette: FUXA library, scene tree, layers, search and ~26 equipment symbols + 7 widget types unreachable
rule_violated: The default editor must expose the same widget/shape palette as the standalone builder; the palette must be a single source of truth that cannot drift from the renderer/symbol registries.
notes: User-reported: shapes present in the SCADA builder are missing in the unified editor.

title: Unified editor HMI properties panel reads the P&ID iframe's processStore selection that ScreenCanvas never sets, so HMI widget config (Config/Alarms/Control/Trends/Events/Animations/Scripts) is unreachable
rule_violated: A widget selected on the active canvas must be editable in the properties panel; selection and edits must target the store the canvas actually writes.
notes: HMI widgets could not be configured from the default editor, including control-security and alarms.

title: Unified editor Undo/Redo and editing keyboard shortcuts are dead no-ops in HMI mode: toolbar targets the undo-less P&ID iframe and useScadaKeyboardShortcuts is never mounted
rule_violated: The default editor must offer working undo/redo and editing shortcuts on the surface being edited; controls must not silently target a hidden or handler-less canvas.
notes: HMI editing had no reachable undo history — a regression from the standalone builder.

title: Unified editor has no in-app play/simulation run mode: the builder's ST-interpreter closed-loop, scenarios, alarm evaluation and HMI animation are unreachable, so a process cannot be run/observed without deploying to a device
rule_violated: The default editor must let users run/simulate a process in-app (edit -> play -> observe) without deploying to hardware, matching the capability the standalone builder already ships.
notes: User-requested FUXA-style in-app run. This closes the HMI run mode; P&ID equipment-node live animation during a run is the tracked follow-on.

title: Late-resolving linked-package query clobbers unsaved HMI edits: the adoption effect only guarded on scadaPackageId, so an in-flight query overwrote in-progress edits and reset isDirty
rule_violated: Data loss: adoption must not overwrite a non-pristine store
notes: Unified editor save/identity integrity.

title: getState timeout silently persists a possibly-stale P&ID snapshot instead of failing the save when the canvas does not respond
rule_violated: The canvas is authoritative at save time; a non-responding canvas must fail the save, not persist a stale mirror
notes: Unified editor save/identity integrity.

title: Repeated saves on a new process spawn duplicate processes because replaceState leaves useParams at new and isNewProcess was OR-ed with id===new
rule_violated: Create-vs-update must be driven by the persisted identity, never the stale route param
notes: Unified editor save/identity integrity.

title: Non-atomic dual-target save marks the process store clean inside its own leg before the package leg, which can throw, leaving process and package out of sync
rule_violated: Both artifacts must be marked clean only after both persist
notes: Unified editor save/identity integrity.

title: SCADA WebSocket control-plane JWT accepts HS256-forged tokens (RS256->HS256 algorithm confusion): a public-key holder can mint an admin token for any tenant and actuate physical outputs via TAG_WRITE
rule_violated: ADR-016: all JWT verification is RS256-only via getJwtVerifyOptions; no per-call algorithms override, no HS256 fallback, especially on a physical-actuation control plane.
notes: Industrial-safety CRITICAL. Fix mirrors the sensor-readings/farm WS gateways; jti-revocation deferred pending token-blacklist keyspace consolidation (SEC-LOW-001/006).

title: SCADA TAG_WRITE is not tenant-fenced and emits a tenant-less write event: a tenant-A socket can actuate tenant-B's device by a predictable deviceCode/localName, and the write is ACKed accepted with no consumer
rule_violated: Every control-plane write must be authorized against the connecting tenant's registry and carry the tenant end-to-end; the ACK must not assert success the backend has not reached.
notes: Industrial-safety CRITICAL. Confirmed-ACK + the cloud->edge tag_write MQTT consumer are the tracked follow-on (no SCADA_TAG_WRITE_EVENT consumer exists yet).

title: Widget control-security (PIN / security level) is client-side theater and the PIN ships plaintext in packageData readable by any tenant member; TAG_WRITE never enforces controlPermissions
rule_violated: Control-security (PIN, security level) must be enforced server-side; secrets must never ship plaintext in client-readable payloads.
notes: TRACKED DEBT (owner auth-security-expert, deadline 2026-08-31): NOT fixed this session — a redaction-only slice makes the client PIN check pass on empty input. Proper fix is a feature: salted pinHash + migration, server-side PIN challenge/response at TAG_WRITE, per-widget controlPermissions enforcement at the gateway. The WS tenant+role+registry gate (SENSOR-CRITICAL-004/005) is the primary control already landed.

title: Multiple SCADA packages can link to one process (no uniqueness on scada_packages.process_id); adoption picks an arbitrary one and orphans the rest
rule_violated: A process links to at most one HMI package; the linkage must be structurally 1:1.
notes: Partial unique index + dedup migration.

title: Unified editor device selector writes local useState instead of the scada store, so meta.edgeDeviceId serializes null and the chosen device is lost on save and reload
rule_violated: Editor selections that belong to the persisted package must be bound to the store, not local component state.
notes: Bind to store targetDeviceId; mark dirty on change.

title: SCADA socket heartbeat watchdog resets only on HEARTBEAT (which the server never pushes), so a healthy socket trips to error after 35s and blocks all operator tag writes
rule_violated: Connection-liveness indicators must reflect the real socket state; a live socket must not be marked disconnected, and write-eligibility must not depend on a broken watchdog.
notes: Reset on any inbound frame + periodic client heartbeat the server echoes.

title: SCADA alarm acknowledgement is a silent no-op: the gateway ALARM_ACK/ALARM_ACK_ALL handlers log but never forward to the alarm engine, so acknowledged alarms stay active
rule_violated: An operator action must reach the authoritative backend state before it is reflected as done; safety-relevant acks must not be no-ops.
notes: Event-based handoff (gateway emits, engine @OnEvent) to avoid the circular DI edge; engine re-broadcasts via pushStatusSummary.

title: All useRealtimeData consumers subscribed under one shared provider id, so mounting/unmounting one widget stomped the others' live tag subscriptions
rule_violated: Concurrent consumers of a ref-counted subscription must each key under their own identity; a shared id makes one consumer's lifecycle silently drop another's subscriptions.
notes: subscribeToTags/unsubscribeFromTags now take a required componentId; useRealtimeData derives it from React.useId(). Simulation provider keeps no-op signatures. Regression test asserts distinct ids + unsubscribe-by-own-id.

title: SCADA design / process / editor-mode zustand singletons are not reset on tenant switch or logout, leaking one tenant's in-progress design into another tenant's session
rule_violated: Tenant-owned client state must be fully cleared on tenant switch and logout so no tenant's data survives into another tenant's session on the same browser.
notes: Co-located registerLogoutCleanup + onTenantChange resets at each store singleton (matching socket/sensor-store convention); added reset action + initial-state constant to editorModeStore. Regression test fires both channels.

title: TagSubscriptionManager.reset() clears local ref-counts without emitting TAG_UNSUBSCRIBE, stranding server-side subscriptions across provider teardown on the shared /scada socket
rule_violated: Client teardown of a shared-socket subscription must notify the server to release those subscriptions; clearing only local state leaks them.
notes: reset() now flushes onFlush([], activeServerTags) before clearing; no-op-safe if the socket is already gone. Two unit tests pin emit-on-active and no-emit-when-empty.

title: Client-writable status on UpdateScadaPackageInput lets a caller forge a PUBLISHED deploy state or un-archive a soft-deleted SCADA package, bypassing the server-owned lifecycle
rule_violated: Lifecycle/deploy state is server-owned; a client update must not be able to set it directly.
notes: Removed status from the update DTO (tier-1: gone from the GraphQL schema) + dropped the service assignment; lifecycle stays with create/deploy/delete. Backend regression spec pins immutability. FE update-input type cleaned too.

title: A soft-deleted (ARCHIVED) SCADA package or process can still be deployed to a live device because no deploy entrypoint checks status before pushing to the edge
rule_violated: A soft-deleted artifact must not be deployable; deploy is a lifecycle transition guarded on status, not an unconditional action.
notes: Shared assertPackageDeployable guard on both package-deploy entrypoints + inline ARCHIVED check in deployProcessToEdge, all before broker publish. Spec covers all three.

title: resolveTagRefs accepts an unbounded refs array that feeds a single IN(...) lookup, a cheap single-query amplification vector at the tenant trust boundary
rule_violated: Untrusted list inputs must be size-bounded before reaching a database query.
notes: Cap at MAX_TAG_REFS_PER_QUERY=1000; BadRequestException before the resolution service. @Args scalar-list args are not covered by ValidationPipe, so the guard is explicit.

title: discoverTags truthiness guard drops zero-valued engineering ranges and alarm limits (engMin=0, alarmL=0) to undefined, losing limits the edge should enforce
rule_violated: Numeric optional values must be null-checked, not truthiness-checked, so zero is preserved.
notes: numberOrUndefined(value != null ? Number(value) : undefined) helper applied to all eng/alarm/deadband fields in discoverTags. Spec pins zero-preservation and null->undefined.

title: createTag/updateTag do not validate fqn against the canonical TagRef grammar, allowing unresolvable ghost registry rows that fail resolution at every deploy/subscribe
rule_violated: An identifier persisted to a registry must be validated against its canonical grammar at the write boundary so it is always resolvable.
notes: @Matches(new RegExp(TAG_REF_PATTERN)) on both fqn DTO fields, reusing the sensor-contracts SSoT pattern. Spec covers create + update, valid + malformed.

title: SCADA package deploy does not gate on unsaved HMI edits, silently shipping the stale server-persisted package while the operator believes current edits were deployed
rule_violated: Deploy ships persisted state; it must refuse (or force a save) when the in-editor artifact has unsaved changes, so the operator never mistakes a stale deploy for their current work.
notes: SCADA deploy gated on scadaDirty (the reliable hydration-guard signal). Process-side dirty-gate deferred + documented: process store isDirty is inaccurate (load marks dirty; load effect re-runs on iframe-ready and races edits) and needs a separate dirty-tracking fix.

title: discoverTags inserts new tags with a plain bulk save that 23505-rolls back the whole batch when a concurrent discovery already created a row, making discovery non-idempotent
rule_violated: Idempotent discovery over a uniquely-keyed set must tolerate concurrent inserts (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), not fail the whole batch on a duplicate.
notes: createQueryBuilder().insert().into(UnifiedTag).values(newTags).orIgnore() then re-read by fqn for the union + ids. createdCount = re-read delta. Spec pins orIgnore + only-new inserted + union returned.

title: ScadaRuntimeModule is never imported by AppModule or any feature module, so the entire /scada WebSocket control plane (gateway, tag manager, alarm engine) is dead code in the running service
rule_violated: A feature module must be reachable from the composition root; an unmounted module is a silently non-functional feature.
notes: AppModule now imports ScadaRuntimeModule. Boot-safety verified (alarm tables migration 1800200000000 exists; 1Hz loop no-op without rules; DAQ lazy). Metadata regression test pins the import.

title: No live-data producer feeds the /scada control plane: gateway.pushTagValues has zero production callers, so subscribed operator screens authenticate, subscribe, and display null forever
rule_violated: A subscription surface that reports connected/healthy must be fed by a real producer; a keyed data plane needs an explicit bridge between its key namespaces.
notes: TagValueFanoutService: registry reverse lookup (TagSource.sensorId/channelId -> fqn, RETIRED excluded) + 60s TTL bounded pos/neg cache + gateway.pushTagValues; wired in NatsIngestionConsumerService.handle after enqueue, never-throws. Population workstream stays SP-001.

title: Unified editor Runtime mode never mounts a live canvas — the center pane is a frozen P&ID iframe fed by nothing, so the mode named Runtime displays no runtime data
rule_violated: A mode that presents itself as live runtime must be wired to the live data plane, not a static rendering.
notes: Runtime now mounts StableModeProvider mode=preview + ScreenCanvas isPreview (LiveDeviceDataProvider, tenant-fenced /scada socket) and hides the still-mounted P&ID iframe. End-to-end with SENSOR-HIGH-045/046.

title: The unified tag registry has no product write path — discover/CRUD hooks and mutations exist with zero consumers, so the registry stays empty and deploy resolution, registry gating, and the live-data fan-out all have nothing to resolve against
rule_violated: A registry that is the SSoT for identity must have a product path to populate and maintain it; defined-but-unmounted mutations are a non-feature.
notes: TagRegistryPage at /sensor/tags: device-scoped Discover, search+paginated browse, field editor, delete-with-confirm, and the live-link (source.sensorId/channelId) editor with sensor+channel pickers (TanStack Query, tenant keys) — completes the discover->link->subscribe->live chain with SENSOR-HIGH-045/046/047.

title: PLC/ST editor Save is a false-success local stub (programs vanish on navigation), Deploy/F9 is inert, and the deploy modal reads the paginated program connection as a bare array so the list is permanently empty
rule_violated: A Save control must persist to the authoritative store before reporting success; a DEPLOYED artifact is immutable and edits must fork; UI reads must match the API contract shape.
notes: persist-mode hydration (lean StPrograms query) + save via create/updateAutomationProgram; DEPLOYED edits fork a new draft; dirty clears only on confirmed write; onDeploy prop wires button+F9 to DeployAutomationModal; modal reads connection.items. Covers UI-001/WF-006/UI-004/UI-005.

title: Tag lifecycle is unreachable — nothing can set RETIRED (dead resolution branch) and deleteTag is an unconditional hard delete that can vanish a tag still referenced by widget bindings
rule_violated: Lifecycle states declared by the schema must be reachable through server-owned transitions; hard delete of a possibly-referenced identity row must be structurally impossible past DRAFT.
notes: retireUnifiedTag mutation (idempotent, revision bump) + DRAFT-only hard delete (ForbiddenException otherwise). FE: status in tag fields, useRetireTag, lifecycle-aware registry actions (draft: delete; active: retire; retired: read-only).

title: Deploy tag resolution is warn-only on all three device-push paths, so packages/processes with unresolvable (unregistered or RETIRED) bindings ship to devices silently
rule_violated: A deploy-boundary validation that only logs is not a gate; unresolvable bindings must block the push, with a controlled rollout for tenants not yet migrated.
notes: SCADA_DEPLOY_TAG_GATE=enforce blocks (BadRequestException naming each unresolved ref) on all 3 paths; default warn preserves pre-backfill tenants. Spec covers enforce-block/warn-proceed/enforce-pass.

title: The atomic two-phase bundle deploy (deployScadaWithAutomation) has zero frontend callers — the unified editor still ships SCADA and automation as separate fire-and-forget deploys, reopening the half-deploy window
rule_violated: When an atomic deploy path exists, the product surface must use it; parallel fire-and-forget deploys of coupled artifacts reintroduce the failure mode the atomic path closes.
notes: useDeployScadaBundle -> deployScadaWithAutomation wired into the unified editor's SCADA deploy dialog; honest staged-awaiting-confirmation success + per-leg failure composition. Bundle stages the SCADA artifact even with zero programs.

title: DAQ history is a success-shaped stub: DAQ_QUERY emits empty results, the scada_tag_history table was never created by any migration, nothing writes history, and the latent schema had no tenant column
rule_violated: A query surface must not report success over a store that does not exist; tenant-scoped telemetry must carry and filter a tenant key on a shared connection.
notes: Migration 1806100000000 (tenant_id NOT NULL, PK tenant+tag+ts, registered in infrastructureTables); tenantId threaded through all DaqStorage methods; gateway streams chunked tenant-fenced results; fan-out persists pushed values; script sandbox passes engine tenant.

title: PLC mode docks the ST editor to the page bottom, cramping the canvas and the editor — product request to present it as a floating popup instead
rule_violated: Product-requested UX: the ST IDE should open as a popup, not occupy the page bottom.
notes: floating presentation prop on StEditorPanel (dock chrome gated to docked mode); PLC mode renders a centered modal overlay; close returns to previous mode. Persistence unchanged (server-side).

title: Process dirty-tracking counts loading as editing and misses real canvas edits (echo-driven), and the process deploy leg has no dirty gate — the Unsaved signal lies both ways and stale saves ship to devices
rule_violated: A dirty flag must derive from user edits, not from hydration echoes; a deploy that ships the server's saved artifact must refuse while unsaved edits exist (WF-004).
notes: Landed: loadProcess reused for one-transaction clean hydration (ProcessHydrationInput); markDirty (identity-idempotent) + startNewProcess(clean); canvas emits canvasEdited from ReactFlow interaction callbacks (position/remove only — programmatic setNodes never fires them); both pages wire canvasEdited/nodeAdded/edgeAdded/delete to markDirty (pid-mode guard, scadaWidget excluded); process deploy leg dirty-gated on both pages, mirroring SENSOR-HIGH-044.

title: Cloud-edge widget-type parity gap: ~53 builder widget types ship into a 16-variant Rust enum with no serde tolerance, so one unfamiliar widget makes the whole package undeployable on the device while the cloud reports success
rule_violated: A publish boundary must ship only what the receiver's contract can parse; the receiver must tolerate unknown enum members instead of failing the whole artifact (CONTRACT-H-002).
notes: Landed: EDGE_SUPPORTED(16)/EDGE_REJECTED(7) rosters + pure transformScadaDocForEdgeDeploy (reject-all-collected, strip decorative, normalize screenType/severity/message); strict EDGE_SCADA_PACKAGE_DOC_SCHEMA recomposed into the publish params schema; both deploy paths transform after upcast (rollback stays byte-faithful); Rust #[serde(other)] Unknown on WidgetType+ScreenType with unknown_widget_count in the deploy ack; all-16 fixture + asymmetric unsupported-widget fixture parity pins; FE Record<ScadaWidgetType,...> partition makes undecided new widget types a compile error.

title: Deleting a SCADA package never removes it from devices: deployed HMIs keep rendering, alarming and actuating from a package the tenant believes deleted (no undeploy command existed; edge clear_package was unreachable and left the SQLite active row)
rule_violated: A destructive lifecycle transition must propagate to every runtime the artifact is deployed on, with honest per-target reporting; deletion that only flips a DB flag is false completion (WF-011).
notes: Landed: undeploy_scada_package contract (schema+fixture+dual parity legs); edge deactivate_package + clear_package SQLite deactivation (fixes restart-resurrection for bundle rollback too) + cmd handler reusing clear_package + dispatch/catalog with DeployProgram RBAC + audit; cloud delete derives devices from deploy logs (latest-row semantics), per-device contract-validated publish with own commandId, UNDEPLOY_SENT/UNDEPLOYED statuses via guarded ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE migration, archive-always best-effort, honest per-device resolver message, ack routing to UNDEPLOYED/FAILED.

title: validatePagination treats an explicit limit of 0 as unset (limit || 20), making its own Math.max(1,...) minimum clamp dead code
rule_violated: An explicit input value must be validated/clamped, not silently coerced to the default; || on numeric inputs conflates 0 with absent.
notes: Landed: null/NaN -> default 20, explicit values clamp 1..100 (mirrors validateLimit). page || 1 untouched (default == min clamp, no observable defect).

title: QUICK_STOP and COAST_STOP are advertised VfdCommandType members with no dispatch case in VfdCommandService - clients sending them get Unknown command
rule_violated: Every member of a client-exposed command enum must dispatch; a non-exhaustive switch over an enum silently strands advertised functionality.
notes: Landed: executeQuickStop (brand QUICK_STOP || CiA402 0x0002) + executeCoastStop (brand COAST || COAST_STOP || 0x0000 OFF2); default arm converted to a compile-time never guard so future enum members cannot silently become Unknown command.

title: SET_FREQUENCY passes any numeric value (600 Hz, -10 Hz) to the physical drive when the speed-reference mapping carries no min/max bounds - the only validation was conditional on nullable columns
rule_violated: A write that actuates physical hardware must be bounds-validated unconditionally; validation gated on optional configuration is fail-open.
notes: Landed: Number.isFinite gate + fallback envelope 0..400 Hz when the mapping is unbounded (widest Hz bound in shipped brand data; min 0 because SET_FREQUENCY is a magnitude). Mapping-configured bounds still win (Rockwell signed -500..500 legitimate). Service remains the single choke point.

title: Seven sensor-service baseline suites shipped red from birth (28 failures): 25 stale/broken tests (wrong literals, vestigial modbus-serial mock vs the raw-net adapter + SSRF guard, unmigrated pooled-connection spec, mutated shared fixture, non-array-aware repo mocks) masked the CI signal and hid three real defects
rule_violated: A permanently-red baseline suite is a disabled CI signal: every new regression drowns in the noise; tests must track deliberate design changes (SSRF guard, connection pooling, batch saves) or be repaired.
notes: Landed: literal fixes (Siemens 9600, CRC 0xCDC5, host message); modbus-tcp spec rebuilt on FakeModbusSocket (net.Socket-only mock, real exports preserved) + SsrfValidatorService prototype spy incl. one unstubbed real-guard test; command spec migrated to pooled/result-object contract + COAST_STOP test; makeProposal() per-test factory; array-aware create/save mocks; assertions target persisted save args. sensor-service now 58/58 suites, 869/869 tests green.

title: Soft-delete on finance_expense_entries + hr_finance_entries records isDeleted/deletedAt but NO deletedBy — the actor who deleted a financial row is unrecoverable, breaking SOC2/GDPR audit attribution
rule_violated: Every destructive action on a regulated (financial) row must record the acting user (deletedBy), not only that it happened.
notes: Wave 1: add deletedBy uuid column (nullable, blue-green migration) to both finance ledger tables and set it in the delete handlers.

title: Manual finance entry batchId/siteId dimensions are accepted as any UUID and stored without an existence/tenant check, so a typo'd or foreign id books a phantom per-batch/per-site cost line
rule_violated: A dimension foreign key on a financial row must reference an existing tenant-owned aggregate; unvalidated dimensions corrupt per-dimension P&L.
notes: Wave 1: validate batchId against batches_v2 and siteId against sites (tenant-scoped) inside the handler transaction before persisting.

title: computedRule JSONB percent is not bounds-validated — a rule with percent outside (0,100] would silently produce a nonsensical computed cost line
rule_violated: A persisted computation parameter must be validated to its legal domain at the boundary that accepts it.
notes: Wave 1: validate the computedRule shape + percent range (0,100] at the evaluator boundary and reject out-of-range rules.

title: HR finance financial mutations (entry/category CRUD, payroll cost settings) carry no @AuditLog, unlike the rest of hr-service, so they are invisible to the platform audit interceptor
rule_violated: Every financial mutation must be captured by the platform audit trail (the @AuditLog + AuditLogInterceptor SSoT hr-service already uses everywhere else).
notes: Wave 1: add @AuditLog to every HR finance mutation resolver.

title: Finance read-model aggregation accumulated money in IEEE-754 float (Number(row.total) + JS + / Math.round), drifting by fractions of a cent across sources/buckets and rounding HALF_UP instead of the platform HALF_EVEN
rule_violated: Monetary accumulation and rounding must be exact (Decimal, HALF_EVEN per the platform Money VO), never IEEE-754 float, even when the wire type stays Float.
notes: Wave 2: the finance ledger query + computed-rule evaluator now accumulate in Decimal.js and round HALF_EVEN, converting to a JS number only at the GraphQL boundary. Per architectural-arbiter ADR-0004 the GraphQL wire scalar (Float->string) is a platform-wide Shared-Kernel change owned by billing-expert + data-expert (tracked separately as DATA-MEDIUM-009, deadline 2026-09-30); finance keeps @Field(Float) and ships only this internal exact-aggregation fix.

title: The MAINTENANCE derived-cost source filters work_orders by COALESCE(completedAt,createdAt) BETWEEN, which no index covers — every finance summary did a full per-tenant work_orders scan
rule_violated: A range-filtered derived-cost date expression must be index-backed; a full source-table scan on every summary load does not hold a p99 budget.
notes: Wave 3: added expression index idx_work_orders_tenant_effective_cost_date on (tenantId, COALESCE(completedAt,createdAt)) via migration 1804800000000. The feeding/harvest/health sources already carry (tenantId,dateColumn) indexes.

title: financeSummary at DAY granularity over a multi-year range emits ~1000+ time-series buckets, each triggering a computed-rule pass and bloating the payload — unbounded server work
rule_violated: Server work and payload for a time series must be bounded regardless of the requested range.
notes: Wave 3: clampGranularity auto-coarsens the granularity so the series never exceeds MAX_SERIES_BUCKETS (400).

title: financeBatchTotals returned one row per batch with no bound — a tenant with thousands of batches ships an unbounded chart payload
rule_violated: A per-dimension chart response must be bounded (top-N with an aggregated remainder), not one row per entity.
notes: Wave 3: getBatchTotals returns the top-N batches by cost (MAX_BATCH_ROWS=25) and rolls the remainder into an 'Other' row.

title: Residual finance FE role-gating: shell nav is not role-filtered for the finance entries, the /finance routes carry no requiredRoles, and hr-module finance buttons are not yet gated
rule_violated: Frontend authz must gate nav visibility and route entry, not only individual action buttons, and must cover every finance surface (farm + hr).
notes: Follow-up to FE-HIGH-060. The FE permission-matrix mirror + useCanMutate button gating for the farm finance surface (create/update/delete entry, category CRUD, archive/restore, settings) is done. Remaining: role-filter the shell nav finance entries, add requiredRoles to the /sites/finance + /hr/finance routes, and gate hr-module finance buttons (needs the HR mutation names in an HR-side matrix, since the shared parity matrix mirrors farm-service only).

title: Every finance mutation invalidated the entire finance query surface ([['finance']]), refetching categories/settings/ledger/summary/batch-totals on any change
rule_violated: A mutation must invalidate only the queries whose data it actually changes, not the whole domain surface.
notes: Wave 3b: scoped invalidation — entry mutations invalidate ledger+summary+batchTotals; category mutations also invalidate the categories catalogue; settings mutations invalidate settings + the currency-dependent aggregates. No mutation refetches the whole finance surface.

title: financeSummary/batchTotals ran 1 manual + N derived grouped queries per load (N+1 DB round-trips)
rule_violated: Aggregation over a fixed source set should compose one DB round-trip, not one query per source.
notes: Wave 3c: single UNION ALL aggregation. buildSummaryAggregationQuery/buildBatchAggregationQuery compose manual + all derived sources into one grouped query (shared $1/$2/$3 params, bound category ids, whitelisted date_trunc unit). Replaces the per-source await loop and aggregateDerivedSource.

title: Finance read path (heaviest farm-service aggregation) had no p99 latency SLO or alert
rule_violated: Every hot-path endpoint must have a p99 latency SLO with an enforcing alert so regressions are detectable, not silent.
notes: Wave 3d: finance p99 SLO. FarmMetricsInterceptor already times queries+mutations into farm_mutation_duration_seconds{operation}, so the finance query series exist. Added recording rule aquaculture:farm_finance_query_latency_p99:5m, alert SloFinanceQueryP99High (>1.5s for 10m), SLI #10 + metric-dependency + rationale in platform-slo.md. Tier-3 detectable.

title: HR labour-cost read model discloses individual salary through small cells: a laborCategory/department with headcount 1-2 exposes an individual's exact (or pair-average) pay
rule_violated: An aggregate salary read must not re-derive an individual's pay through a cell too small to anonymise; employee.baseSalary is @HideField() precisely to keep individual pay unqueryable.
notes: Wave 4: k-anonymity threshold (SMALL_CELL_MIN_HEADCOUNT=3) in the pure LabourCostCalculator + department merge. Salary of a cell with 0<headcount<k is withheld (null + salarySuppressed flag), headcount kept; complementary suppression prevents a lone small cell being recovered from the published grand total; UI renders a dash.

title: HR per-department expense double-count: null-departmentHrId employees fan out into multiple enum-department rows that each read the single 'none' expense bucket, attributing the whole unassigned-expense pool to every row (+ expenses for departments with no active employees are dropped)
rule_violated: A per-group financial breakdown must attribute each amount to exactly one group; salaries and expenses must aggregate on the same grouping key.
notes: Wave 4: employees grouped by departmentHrId only (one null 'Unassigned' row, not per-enum fan-out); pure mergeDepartmentCosts joins salary+expenses on the single key so each expense is counted once and an expense-only department surfaces instead of being dropped. Unit-tested (merge-department-costs.spec).
