title: Work identity is cycle-scoped and the candidate generator has no production caller: task.py derives task_id from cycle_id, so the same defect rediscovered on a later night is a new task with no history, and generate_task_candidates - the only thing that would turn discovery into tracked work - is never called by production code
rule_violated: No plan may silently go half-done - the program's first rule - is unenforceable without a durable subject to enforce it against. _task_id(cycle_id, source, source_id) makes identity a function of WHEN the work was seen rather than WHAT it is, so nothing accumulates evidence, nothing resumes after a crash, and a mission cannot carry a retry ladder or a wake condition across the cycle boundary. The generator compounds it: machinery that exists and is never called is the defect class six of Wave 1's seven PRs closed.
notes: Wave 2 PR 1.1 of docs/plans/2026-08-02-aria-full-autonomy-program/PLAN.md. The IDENTITY half closes in the registering commit: mission_id = m-sha256(source_kind|source_id|repo_hash)[:16] with no timestamp, counter or cycle reference, so the same source re-observed in any later cycle folds into the same mission. Pinned by an AST test rather than a behavioural one because a time component would collide within one second and pass a same-run equality check - test_mission_id_source_never_reads_cycle_or_time walks the module source and refuses any mission-id function referencing cycle identity or any freshness source (clock, uuid, randomness). The NO-PRODUCTION-CALLER half stays open until PR 1.2 wires the mission_ingest phase as the first production caller of task.generate_task_candidates; this finding tracks both halves until then rather than being split, because closing it on identity alone would record the harder half as done. Vocabularies (9 mainline + 5 interim + 5 terminal states, transition edges, retry ladder, wake kinds, binding keys, event kinds) are closed tables in mission.py and nowhere else, with one stated exception: a forward mainline skip is legal only under reason_code=coarse_observation, because today's pipeline genuinely cannot distinguish every intermediate state and a skip that says so is honest where a skip wearing a precise reason would be the schema lying about its own resolution. Interim states sit outside ACTIVE_WIP_STATES on purpose so a mission waiting on a human releases its WIP slot instead of deadlocking the pipeline. title: The ARIA kernel suite writes into the host repository when it inherits GIT_DIR: cwd= selects the work tree but GIT_DIR selects the repository, so every fixture that carefully passed cwd=<tempdir> still ran git init, git config, git add and git commit against the developer's real checkout - and the pre-push hook that runs the suite is itself launched by git, which exports GIT_DIR
rule_violated: A gate must not damage the thing it guards. git exports an absolute GIT_DIR into its own environment whenever the git dir is not the default .git in cwd, which is always true inside a linked worktree; git push therefore hands GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name> to .husky/pre-push, which hands it to scripts/ci/aria-suite-changed.mjs, which forwards process.env verbatim to the Python suite. apply_hermetic_git_env redirected GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM and claimed that made ambient leakage structurally impossible for every fixture in the process - but it never touched the variable family that decides WHICH REPOSITORY a git subprocess acts on, so the guarantee was narrower than its own docstring.
notes: Observed live, not hypothesised: a push from a linked worktree ran the pre-push suite and mutated the real repository - core.bare=true (git guesses BARE because the exported GIT_DIR ends in the worktree name rather than /.git, and for a linked worktree git_path(config) resolves through commondir to the MAIN .git/config), user.email=fixture@aria.test and user.name='Aria Fixture', gc.auto=0 / gc.autoDetach=false / maintenance.auto=false, remote.origin.url rewritten to the fixture literal at tests/test_phase3_discovery_mfe.py, about twelve stray commits (fixture: initial commit, fixture: seed N files, init, initial), files x.ts and src/a.ts staged onto the real index, branches aria/feature-test, aria/executor-fixture, aria/fixture-proposal-<id> and fixture-wt, and worktree registrations pointing into /tmp. The three keys gc.auto, gc.autoDetach and maintenance.auto are written by exactly three lines in the entire codebase (git_fixtures.py:58-60), which identifies the factory beyond doubt. Under explicit GIT_DIR with no GIT_WORK_TREE, git's setup_explicit_git_dir falls through to set_git_work_tree(cwd), so git add <rel> reads the temp file and stages it into the REAL index at that relative path. FIXED at tier 1 in the registering commit: apply_hermetic_git_env now REMOVES the nine repo-location variables (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES, GIT_NAMESPACE, GIT_PREFIX) rather than overriding them, because there is no value for GIT_DIR meaning 'use the directory I am standing in' - absence is the only way to say it. Scrubbed at process start via tests/__init__.py so it covers every fixture, factory-built or inline, instead of a discipline each of the ~30 inline call sites must remember. hermetic_git_env_is_active now includes absence in its definition so the predicate cannot answer 'hermetic' while GIT_DIR points at the host repo. Three new invariants I-HERM-07/08/09; I-HERM-09 reproduces the incident end to end in a child process and mutation-checking confirms it fails when the scrub is removed. title: Four HIGH advisories in production dependencies turn security-scan red and block every merge platform-wide: brace-expansion DoS, fast-uri host confusion, ip-address SSRF/trust-boundary bypass (3 CVEs), socket.io-parser memory exhaustion - and the override that should fix brace-expansion under minimatch does not take effect
rule_violated: security-scan runs npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev and feeds the required build-status check, so a newly published advisory in a transitive production dependency halts every merge in the repository until it is resolved. Three of the four resolve cleanly by raising existing override floors; the fourth does not, which means the repository has no working mechanism to pin that transitive package.
notes: Diagnosed but NOT fixed - recorded so the blockage is tracked rather than rediscovered. All four are transitive (isDirect false). THREE FIX CLEANLY by raising floors that already exist in package.json overrides: fast-uri ^3.1.4 -> ^3.1.5, ip-address ^10.2.0 -> ^10.4.0 (vulnerable range is <=10.3.0, so the obvious ^10.3.1 is NOT enough), and a new socket.io-parser ^4.2.7; that combination also clears nx's brace-expansion copy. THE FOURTH RESISTS: node_modules/minimatch/node_modules/brace-expansion stays at 5.0.8. minimatch@10.2.5 requests ^5.0.5, 5.0.9 is published, and the existing override key minimatch@^10 -> brace-expansion is demonstrably the key that produced 5.0.8 from ^5.0.8 - yet raising it to ^5.0.9 leaves 5.0.8 in place, including after deleting package-lock.json and re-resolving from scratch. A version-range override key (brace-expansion@>=4.0.0 <5.0.9) does not help either, because npm matches override keys against the spec a PARENT REQUESTS, not against the resolved version. A blanket brace-expansion override is the wrong instrument: the tree carries safe 1.1.15/2.1.1/2.1.2 copies under eslint, glob and others that a 5.x override would major-bump. Likely next step is bumping minimatch itself, since 10.2.5 is what pulls a vulnerable floor. notes: VfdAutomationRuleService.onSensorReading(event: SensorReadingEvent) is a complete implementation - it finds matching rules, evaluates conditions and creates change sets - reached by nothing. The method carries no @OnEvent, no @EventPattern and no bus subscription, and a tree-wide grep finds zero callers outside its own file. A tenant can therefore create an automation rule ('when dissolved oxygen drops below X, raise the aerator to Y Hz'), see it listed as ACTIVE, and it will never fire. This is not the same defect as SENSOR-HIGH-067 (no telemetry poller): that one is about reading FROM drives, this is about reacting to sensor readings by writing TO them. Both are reachability holes on the same surface, which is why the VFD module looks complete and does nothing. Fix direction: subscribe the handler on the sensor-reading subject the alert engine already consumes and return a HandlerOutcome (PLAT-HIGH-902 contract), rather than adding a second private dispatch path. Deliberately out of scope of the VFD reachability PR that registered it: that PR fixes the surfaces a human operates (activation, device selection, panel mounting, channel CRUD); wiring an autonomous write path to live sensor readings is a separate blast radius that needs its own review and its own tests. [canonicalize-owner 2026-10-18: owner_user okan -> Okan-wqm — ARIA-MEDIUM-535 owner identity is the CODEOWNERS handle]

title: The SCADA VFD drive widget binds its device by free-text id and its start/stop/program buttons are dropped by the node's command dispatcher, so the widget renders controls that do nothing at runtime
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a control that cannot perform its action must not be rendered as if it can
notes: Two independent halves. (1) VfdDriveWidgetConfig asks for the VFD device by a plain <input type="text"> labelled 'VFD Device ID' with placeholder 'Enter VFD device ID...', so binding a widget requires a human to paste a UUID copied from elsewhere; a typo binds the widget to nothing and reads as an empty drive. Every other device-bound surface in the module selects from a device list. (2) VfdDriveWidget's start/stop/program buttons call onCommand('vfd:start'|'vfd:stop'|'vfd:program') and are enabled only when !isEditing - that is, only at runtime - but ScadaWidgetNode.handleCommand branches on 'navigate' and, in simulation mode only, 'toggle'/'press'/'writeTag'. The three vfd: commands match no branch, there is no else and no warning: the click is swallowed. An operator on a SCADA screen presses Stop on a running drive and gets no error and no effect. Registered rather than fixed in the VFD reachability PR because a real fix issues a VFD command from a SCADA runtime surface, which needs the command authorization and audit path reviewed on its own - a silent no-op is safer than an unaudited write, but it must not stay silent: the minimum correct interim behaviour is to disable the buttons, which is itself part of the fix and not a workaround. [canonicalize-owner 2026-10-18: owner_user okan -> Okan-wqm — ARIA-MEDIUM-535 owner identity is the CODEOWNERS handle]

title: A data channel's operationalMin/operationalMax gate every reading through validateValue but no GraphQL type reads or writes them, so a manually created channel has no operational band and no way to get one
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach: a column that changes runtime behaviour must have a defined way to be set, or it is state nothing can reach
notes: Surfaced while fixing SENSOR-HIGH-063 and NOT asserted to be a live break - it may well be the intended design. operationalMin/operationalMax are distinct from minValue/maxValue: the latter is the physical range, the former the operational band SensorDataChannel.validateValue rejects readings against (:408-411) with a reason string (:433). They are populated in exactly one place, sensor-type.service.ts:347-348, from a sensor-type template's channel definitions. Neither CreateDataChannelInput, UpdateDataChannelInput nor the DataChannelType output object mentions them, so a channel created through the channel manager - the only manual path - is born with no operational band and can never be given one; its readings skip that validation entirely while a template-provisioned channel's do not. Two readings of this are possible and the finding does not pick one: either the operational band is deliberately template-owned (in which case the gap is that nothing says so, and a manual channel silently opts out of a safety check), or it is user config that was never wired (in which case the input types are missing three fields). Deciding needs product intent, which is why this is registered rather than fixed inside a CRUD repair. The FE had been sending the editor's PHYSICAL range under these names, so nothing was ever written to them from the UI even before the request started failing. [canonicalize-owner 2026-10-18: owner_user okan -> Okan-wqm — ARIA-MEDIUM-535 owner identity is the CODEOWNERS handle]

Verified on nats:2.10.24: create with a differing config → 10148; consumers.update() → OK and the ack position survives; identical create is idempotent; a non-updatable change (deliver_policy) → 10012, still loud. The library cannot send the empty create-or-update action (opts.action || 'create'), so the bus creates, and on 10148 updates by durable name.

title: farm-service cannot boot: three source-schema tables recorded as migrated (feeding_record_attribution_quarantine template, tenant_localization, feeding_job_runs) no longer exist, so the SchemaDriftValidator refuses the cold start; the migration ledger and the schema disagree and no migration re-aligns them
rule_violated: ADR-012 schema drift: the DB is aligned to the entities by a migration (docs/runbooks/schema-drift-response.md path a); a recorded migration whose objects are gone is drift the ledger cannot see.
notes: Release e9fd27bf3: 15/16 services healthy, aqua-farm fatal on schema.drift.detected (3 violations). db-migrate had logged 'absentTables: [feeding_record_attribution_quarantine]' every run and proceeded. Cause (mechanism verified in schema-manager.service.ts): SourceSchemaBootstrapService in strict mode DROP…CASCADEs source tables its own image's MODULE_SCHEMAS does not list; 2026-09-17 locally built farm images from an older branch reaped the three newest farm tables as orphans (tenant clones untouched). Fix: two new migrations recreate them IF NOT EXISTS (per-tenant template unqualified + fan-out; infrastructure ledgers schema-qualified + @SourceOnlyMigration), proven on a throwaway Postgres shaped like production: all three restored, tenant clone and rows untouched, template columns identical to the clone, idempotent.

title: SourceSchemaBootstrapService (strict mode) DROP…CASCADEs every source-schema table absent from the RUNNING image's MODULE_SCHEMAS: starting any older image against a newer database destroys the tables the newer migrations created, while their migration rows stay recorded — the mechanism that removed farm's three feeding ledgers on 2026-09-17
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md tier 1 (make it impossible): a runtime that destroys data the migration authority created is a second, unversioned writer of the schema; db-migrate is the DDL authority (ADR-011/012). Orphan handling must be non-destructive (quarantine/rename or refuse to boot), and a table created by a migration the ledger records must never count as an orphan.
notes: Shape of the fix: the bootstrap consults the schema's migration ledger (a table whose creating migration is recorded is never an orphan) and, for genuine orphans, renames into a quarantine namespace or fails closed with a drift alert instead of dropping; db-migrate treats absentTables for recorded migrations as a hard failure rather than a log line, so the ledger/schema disagreement stops the deploy before a service refuses to boot.

title: Three farm source-schema tables are missing although their creating migrations (1808700000000, 1809100000000) are recorded with passing postConditions — cause not established — and nothing between db-migrate and service health detects a database that no longer matches the entities: the deploy fails at the service's cold start twenty minutes after the migration step said it was done
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md tier 3 (make it detectable) and ADR-012: schema drift is validated at each service's cold start, but the migration authority that could stop the deploy runs no drift check itself; a ledger/schema disagreement therefore surfaces as a health failure, not as a failed migration step.
notes: Supersedes DATA-HIGH-017, which attributed the loss to SourceSchemaBootstrapService dropping unregistered source tables; on main that service throws (assertNoOrphanTables) and the DROP…CASCADE was removed in 42695736f (2026-06-08), before either migration existed — the schema-manager.service.ts docblock describing the drop is stale text. Established: ledger rows exist, the quarantine table exists only in the tenant clone, the two clock ledgers exist nowhere, no db-migrate run since 2026-09-17 logged a drop, and the applying run's container is gone. Candidates: the source pass executed under a tenant-first search_path, or a manual drop. Detectable fix: db-migrate runs the SchemaDriftValidator for every service after its migrations and fails the run — and the deploy — when the database is unlike the entities; plus absentTables for a recorded migration becomes a hard failure rather than a log line. Restoration itself: FARM-CRITICAL-332.

title: The droplet deploy contract is unsatisfiable: sensor-ingestion is catalogued `required` while the deploy never ships its image (rust-sidecar excluded from the image matrix, compose pins it to the deploy's ${TAG}, droplet-up neither pulls nor starts it) — every release ledger since 2026-08-28 reads failed/required_health and promotion is blocked
rule_violated: A criticality level is a promise the post-deploy health gate enforces; it may only be made for a service the deploy can place on the host. No invariant related the catalog's criticality to the image matrix, so the 2026-08-28 'honesty flip' to required went green in CI and red on every droplet run.
notes: Runs 35514785422 and 35520382281 (2026-09-20): `[required] sensor-ingestion — container not found` → `Required service health check failed. Promotion blocked without automatic rollback`, `status=failed phase=required_health` — with 16/16 real services healthy and login working. Fix: criticality 'warning' (the truthful deploy promise today) and `deployShipsImage()` in the catalog with a parity invariant that fails any critical/required active droplet entry whose image the deploy does not build or pull; the sidecar pin now expects 'warning'. Actually shipping the sidecar (own SENSOR_INGESTION_TAG, pull + start in droplet-up, health) is the tracked follow-up that lifts it back to 'required'.

title: required-signals.yaml asserts a boot signal for sensor-ingestion, a service the deploy never ships — the same unsatisfiable promise DEPLOY-HIGH-024 removed from the health gate, through the boot-signal gate: run 35529464872 passed health, failed `phase=boot_signal` on `[sensor-ingestion] nats_auth_mode_mtls` and rolled back
rule_violated: A deploy gate may only assert what the deploy can observe; the required-signals artifact was derived from `requiredSignals` alone, ignoring whether the service's image ever reaches the host. DEPLOY-HIGH-024 introduced `deployShipsImage()` for the criticality contract but did not apply it to the sibling contract.
notes: Deploy 8c9795f3 (2026-09-20 19:30Z): `all critical/required services satisfied`, then `Missing boot signals: [sensor-ingestion] nats_auth_mode_mtls` → `Boot signal assertion failed. Initiating rollback` → ledger `rolled_back phase=boot_signal`; the droplet stayed on 8c9795f3 and healthy (login OK). Fix: the generator derives the manifest only from entries `deployShipsImage()` accepts, and the parity invariant asserts an un-shipped service is absent from it (sensor-ingestion pinned absent).

title: NatsV3Client.publish() builds the reply inbox from the registration option alone (`createInbox(this.options.inboxPrefix)`), so every ClientProxy without an explicit prefix subscribes the default `_INBOX.<nuid>` — refused under the identity-scoped grants (INFRA-HIGH-179) — and no platform request/reply through the proxy receives its answer
rule_violated: ADR-015: the reply inbox is a property of the identity on the wire (cert CN), decided by the connection factory; a second, registration-time decision that can disagree with it must not exist. INFRA-HIGH-179 scoped the factory and the grants but left the proxy's own createInbox() on the registration option — the unit spec covered the factory, no test drove publish().
notes: aqua-nats after the 8c9795f3 deploy, 19:37:00–01Z: ten `Subscription Violation - User "CN=gateway_service", Subject "_INBOX.XqtwFWfJUUH15AE22mf…"` in one second — the gateway's WebSocket RPCs (verifyMembership, verifyDeviceOwnership, request.ai.chat) subscribing the ungranted default root; the same path serves admin-api (6 clients), messaging (5), ai, hr, sensor. Latent since #1637 replaced `_INBOX.>` with `_INBOX<IDENTITY>.>`; HTTP/GraphQL login was unaffected, so it survived every probe today. Fix: the client captures the prefix the factory put on the connection at connect() (registration override kept for the separately granted `_INBOXBILLINGCFG` / `_INBOXFARMMARINECFG` channels) and publish() creates every inbox under it; a spec drives the real publish() through a stubbed transport and fails on the `_INBOX.` root.

title: The reply leg of every request/reply is refused under the scoped inbox grants: a requester's inbox is `_INBOX<ITS CN>.<nuid>` but no responder holds a publish grant for another identity's inbox root (only `_INBOX.>`), so the broker logs `Publish Violation` at the responder and the caller times out — proven on nats:2.10.24 with main's conf
rule_violated: ADR-015: the generated authorization block must let an identity complete the protocols its grants imply; scoping the requester's inbox (INFRA-HIGH-179) without a reply mechanism for responders left request/reply half-granted. Nothing exercised a two-identity round trip against the generated conf.
notes: Found by aqua-saas-0a's live-broker probe after #1654 (publish to `_INBOXGATEWAY_SERVICE.probe` as auth_service → Publish Violation) and reproduced on a throwaway nats:2.10.24 with main's nats.conf: gateway_service → messaging_service `request.messaging.verifyMembership` times out with one `Publish Violation - User "CN=messaging_service", Subject "_INBOXGATEWAY_SERVICE.<nuid>.<n>"`. Only the two config-reply prefixes worked because config_service holds explicit `_INBOXBILLINGCFG.>`/`_INBOXFARMMARINECFG.>` publish grants. Fix: the generator emits `allow_responses: { max: 64, expires: "5m" }` for every user — a responder may publish only to the reply subject of a request it received; same probe on the new conf: reply lands, zero violations. Invariant: every generated user block carries exactly one allow_responses. The blanket `_INBOX.>` publish grants are now inert (no one subscribes that root) and stay until a separate tightening.

The page now derives the currency from byCurrency: with exactly one it formats in THAT currency through formatCurrencyAmount; with more than one the cross-currency sums are rendered as an em dash and the real per-currency figures are listed instead, which are the numbers an operator can act on. Second: 'Payments With Refunds' fetched getPayments({status:'succeeded', limit:100}) and counted the rows whose refundedAmount exceeded zero, presenting that count beside 'Successful Payments' which was the endpoint's true total — a subtotal over at most a hundred rows next to a platform figure. Fixing SENSOR-CRITICAL-190 restores the SENSOR-CRITICAL-086 contract, no PUBACK without the durable commit, and with it the loop that contract always had for a deterministic failure. The panel's payload cases (a nanosecond ts, deep nesting, a non-scalar channel value) are fixed in that change, which makes the listener code inside the durable leg total; what remains is a permanent database error. Failure scenario: one tenant's sensor_metrics drifts from the columns the writer inserts (SQLSTATE 42703), or a channel row breaks a constraint. Its next reading fails the tenant transaction, dispatchDurable force-reconnects, the broker redelivers that message first, and because mqtt.js 5.15.1 sends PUBACK and takes the next inbound packet only from the handleMessage callback (build/lib/handlers/publish.js:87-91), every tenant's readings queue behind it until the broker's queue overflows. The only signals are an error log line per attempt and sensor_mqtt_messages_failed_total. Prod recorded zero sensor_mqtt_messages_failed_total increments over the 15-day Prometheus retention (2026-10-02 to 2026-10-18, about 58,900 messages a week), so the class is latent today. SENSOR-HIGH-093 (Step 1.6, no owner, no deadline) is the NATS-consumer DLQ and replay; this row is the MQTT ack gate's half of the same step. A fix classifies a durable-leg failure: transient (connection loss, SQLSTATE 08, 40, 53, 57, 58, timeouts) stays unacked for redelivery; permanent is written to a per-tenant quarantine row and acked; an alert fires on sensor_mqtt_messages_failed_total. Round-2 verification (2026-10-18): the lookup leg has the same class. findSensorByTopic reloads the sensor on every message, before the write, and a failed reload becomes DurableWriteError. A reload that fails because the tenant is gone (db-migrate's delete job dropped its schema, so the tenant boundary raises SCHEMA_MISMATCH) is now 'found nothing' in LW-SENSOR-ACK: the tenant is not in platform.list_active_tenant_schema_mappings(), so its topic mappings are evicted and the reading is acked and dropped. A reload that fails the same way on every attempt for a tenant that is still active stays in this row. Lookup-leg failure scenario: one tenant's per-tenant migration fails and its sensors table lacks a column the Sensor entity selects; its next reading's reload raises 42703, the gate force-reconnects, and the broker redelivers that message first, as for the write leg. The transient/permanent classifier this row asks for covers both the lookup and the write leg. Correction to the prod figure above: on main a failed lookup returned null and was counted as processed, not failed, so the 15-day zero of sensor_mqtt_messages_failed_total covers write-leg failures only and says nothing about lookup failures. [canonicalize-owner 2026-10-18: owner_user okan -> Okan-wqm — ARIA-MEDIUM-535 owner identity is the CODEOWNERS handle]

title: sensor-service publishes its four automation events on type-first subjects (events.<Type>.<tenant>) while services.yaml grants events.*.<Type> and gateway-api subscribes events.<Type>.>, so the publishes fall outside the grant and the gateway's filters overlap every events.*.<T> subject

title: No test drives the executor drain that is chained after a night held on a provider outage: no claim, no requeue charge, and at most one re-probe per provider are unproven for that drain
rule_violated: Every guarantee is backed by a test (ARIA-HIGH-579 operator decision 2026-10-17: a held night claims and charges nothing)
notes: Raised by the review of ARIA-HIGH-579 (minor, 'the executor half of claims nothing is unproven'). Not fixed on fix/aria-579-hold-in-place. The reviewer's first fix option, stopping the drain at fleet_outage, is wrong after the review's major fix: provider_hold now holds a night on an open outage whose lapsed policy back-off a waiting request will re-probe, and the chained and 02:29 drains' native admission is the lane that re-probes it and, through the served spawn, restores it. A drain that stopped at the fleet outage would leave the hold standing for ever. Fix: add a scenario step that runs ci_executor_drain.drain_pending after a held night on the same store, with the admission's probes stubbed. Pin three things: each waiting request is refused or admitted by native admission with no claim charged; a provider with a lapsed back-off is probed at most once per drain, because the refusal renews its back-off; and a 200 admits, so the served spawn's record_provider_restored ends the hold for the next night.

title: Ordinary certificate renewal regenerates the internal CA: droplet-up.sh passes --force when the redis leaf is inside 30 days of expiry, and --force also mints a new CA, so restarted services trust a root the running NATS broker does not hold
evidence: scripts/deploy/droplet-up.sh:1009 (runs generate-internal-certs.sh --force when CERT_RENEW is set at :1002-1004: the redis server leaf has under 30 days left)
infrastructure/docker/scripts/generate-internal-certs.sh:29 (--force sets FORCE=true, the generator's only renewal switch)
infrastructure/docker/scripts/generate-internal-certs.sh:603-626 (the CA is kept only when FORCE=false; with --force it mints a new ca-key.pem and ca-cert.pem and publishes both by rename)
docker-compose.droplet.yml:631-633 (NATS bind-mounts nats-cert.pem, nats-key.pem and ca-cert.pem as single files: the running broker keeps the inodes it started with)
scripts/deploy/droplet-up.sh:508 (an application rollout recreates NATS only when nats.conf changed; the re-pinned checkout keeps unchanged files' mtime, scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh:123)
rule_violated: A leaf renewal keeps the trust root every running consumer already holds; replacing the CA is a separate, explicit operation that certificate expiry can never select.
notes: Lost-work audit 2026-10-16, 'Re-land first' item 1 (CRITICAL). The old branch fix/login-permanent-recovery (commit 57ca1a0f3, PR #1452 closed unmerged) carried this as ORPHAN-CRITICAL-820. That id is not in main's registry, and the old row's title names the PostgreSQL-mount half, so this is a fresh row. Re-verified on origin/main 5d886865a with throwaway certificates: --force replaced both ca-key.pem and ca-cert.pem. Failure scenario: the first application rollout after 2027-04-28 (the live redis and nats leaves expire 2027-05-28) runs --force. Restarted services mount the new CA copy and new client leaves, while the running broker keeps the old CA and the old server leaf. Every restarted service then fails the TLS handshake in both directions, and a rollback restores the images but not the old CA. The PostgreSQL-mount half of the old row is ORPHAN-CRITICAL-810 (OPEN on main) and is not part of this row. [canonicalize-owner 2026-10-19: owner_user okan -> Okan-wqm — ARIA-MEDIUM-535 owner identity is the CODEOWNERS handle]

title: The certificate generator's key-pair and CA validators return success on an unparseable certificate or key: a bare return after a failed `if ! x=$(...)` returns 0, so a default run logs the error, prints [skip] and exits 0
evidence: infrastructure/docker/scripts/generate-internal-certs.sh:283-284 (validate_certificate_key_pair returns the status of the negated test, 0, when the certificate subject cannot be read; the same at :291-292 and :294-295 for the key and certificate digests)
infrastructure/docker/scripts/generate-internal-certs.sh:316-317 (validate_certificate_authority has the same three bare returns, also at :324-325 and :327-328)
infrastructure/docker/scripts/generate-internal-certs.sh:485-490 (the skip path trusts that status: an unparseable nats-cert.pem logs '[skip] nats' and the run exits 0)
rule_violated: A validator that reports an error fails: a certificate-store check that cannot parse an identity refuses the run before any consumer is recreated.
notes: Found while re-landing the CA-renewal fix (lost-work item 1). The old branch fix/login-permanent-recovery changed these returns in 57ca1a0f3 without a row of their own. Reproduced on origin/main 5d886865a with throwaway certificates: with 'garbage' in nats/nats-cert.pem a default run printed 'nats server certificate is not a parseable X.509 certificate', then '[skip] nats', and exited 0. Effect: the deploy preflight passes, and NATS fails when its container starts, after production state has changed. [canonicalize-owner 2026-10-19: owner_user okan -> Okan-wqm — ARIA-MEDIUM-535 owner identity is the CODEOWNERS handle]

title: A renewed leaf never reaches a consumer the rollout does not recreate: renewal re-issues every server and client leaf, but a selective rollout recreates only the services it rolls out and NATS only when nats.conf changed, so the broker, PostgreSQL and every other service keep their old leaf until it expires
evidence: infrastructure/docker/scripts/generate-internal-certs.sh:828 (once any managed leaf is inside 30 days of expiry, the deploy's generator run renews every server and client leaf in one run)
docker-compose.droplet.yml:631-633 (NATS bind-mounts its server leaf, key and CA copy as single files: a leaf published by rename is not the inode the running broker opened)
docker-compose.droplet.yml:173-202 (each application service bind-mounts its own client leaf and key as single files in the same way)
docker-compose.droplet.yml:369-371 (PostgreSQL bind-mounts its server leaf and CA copy as single files in the same way)
scripts/deploy/droplet-up.sh:508-511 (ensure_nats_acl_loaded keeps the broker when nats.conf's hash matches and its mtime predates the container start; the TLS files are not compared)
scripts/deploy/droplet-up.sh:1475 (a selective rollout reaches that check only when RUN_DB_MIGRATE=true)
scripts/deploy/droplet-up.sh:1479 (a selective rollout recreates only restartable_deploy_services, the services it rolls out)
scripts/deploy/droplet-up.sh:1438 (a production selective rollout runs up -d postgres redis minio, which keeps an unchanged container; a development rollout preserves them at :1433)
scripts/deploy/droplet-up.sh:1162 (only the full-stack path removes every container, after which each consumer opens the renewed files)
rule_violated: A renewed identity is in force on every consumer before the identity it replaces expires: a deploy that renews leaves recreates every consumer of a renewed leaf, or renews only on a path that recreates everything.
notes: Found while re-landing the CA-renewal fix (lost-work item 1); not fixed by it. Widened before merge after the change's verification round 1: the first text of this row named only the NATS server leaf and a development-only PostgreSQL gap. Once the CA is kept, restarted services still trust the old leaves, so nothing fails on the renewal day; every old leaf expires at most 30 days later. Failure scenario: renewal runs in a selective rollout, and no full-stack deploy (FULL_DEPLOY=true without preserved data infrastructure) follows within 30 days. The broker then presents an expired server leaf to every NATS client, and every service the rollout did not restart presents an expired client leaf to the broker. PostgreSQL presents an expired server leaf too; the applications run DATABASE_SSL=false, so that impact is low. A nats.conf change recreates only the broker. The live leaves expire 2027-05-28, so renewal starts with the first deploy after 2027-04-28. [canonicalize-owner 2026-10-19: owner_user okan -> Okan-wqm — ARIA-MEDIUM-535 owner identity is the CODEOWNERS handle]

title: An ordinary certificate run into an empty store mints a new CA while the NATS broker and PostgreSQL still run on the old one, so a selective rollout splits every restarted service from them
evidence: infrastructure/docker/scripts/generate-internal-certs.sh:881-899 (with no CA and no managed leaf, key or CA copy in the store, the no-option run mints a new CA and publishes it by rename; nothing compares it with the root the running consumers hold)
scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh:74 (DEPLOY_CERTS_DIR defaults to ${DEPLOY_SOURCE_REPO}/certs, so overriding DEPLOY_SOURCE_REPO or DEPLOY_CERTS_DIR points the deploy at another store)
scripts/deploy/deploy-paths.sh:137 (mkdir -p creates that store, empty, when it does not exist)
scripts/deploy/droplet-up.sh:1002 (the deploy runs the generator with no option and continues on exit 0)
scripts/deploy/droplet-up.sh:1479 (a selective rollout recreates only the services it rolls out; ensure_nats_acl_loaded at :508-511 keeps a broker whose nats.conf is unchanged)
rule_violated: A deploy never publishes a trust root that a consumer it leaves running does not hold: a CA is minted only when no running consumer holds another root, or on a path that recreates every consumer.
notes: Found by the LW-CA-REGEN security verification (round 2, probe P3, chain/items/LW-CA-REGEN/verify-security-2/probe.log; raised again in run R12, probe P7 of verify-security-r12-2) and not fixed by the INFRA-CRITICAL-233 change. That change makes a partly wiped store refuse (the branch at :874, before :881), but a store with no managed file at all keeps main's behavior, and certificate expiry cannot select this path. Failure scenario: DEPLOY_SOURCE_REPO or DEPLOY_CERTS_DIR is overridden, or the store is wiped. deploy-paths.sh creates an empty store, the generator exits 0 with '[done] CA', and a selective rollout restarts only the services it rolls out. Their new leaves chain to a root the running broker does not trust, so every restarted service fails the NATS handshake, and the broker's leaf fails theirs. Suggested direction: droplet-up.sh refuses a run whose generator minted a CA while any aqua- container is running, unless it takes the full-stack path. First minted as INFRA-HIGH-236 in an unpushed commit whose anchors the follow-up change moved; that row never landed, so the id 236 is reserved with no row.

title: About 21 aria-kernel test sites create a temp tree with tempfile.mkdtemp and never remove it (test_typed_verdict_bridge, test_cli_profile_commands, test_doctor, v3_2 phase invariants, ...), the class ARIA-LOW-595 closed for test_published_text

title: The skill-genesis drainer authors an operator seed with no sane calibration corpus through the evidence-pack proxy, spending a drafting round on a run whose sandbox can only end sandbox_systematic_failure

Fix direction: every adapter-controlled row field bounded by construction (ARIA-HIGH-618's artifact move with byte-bounded samples, ARIA-MEDIUM-619) plus a pin test of a week of maximal rows under the cap, or a publish compaction that brings the window under budget (the wave-3 bucket's test_publish_bound_holds_for_a_week_of_full_breadth_runs, ported onto read_paths_ref). rule_violated: A published surface's size does not depend on what an adapter chooses to print: every writer of a published file is bounded at write time against the publish cap, and a run whose evidence cannot fit is recorded with its bulk spilled, never written in a shape that refuses every later publish (order map SUP-01).

The class is on origin/main: a budget_exceeded run with 70 MiB of stdout writes a 73,401,132-byte hot artifact (probe_stdout_artifact.main.70.out), over the 67,108,864-byte cap. ARIA-HIGH-617's payload.scope_violations lowers the threshold for parsed runs: with stdout just under 12 MiB and every path out of scope, 5 non-ASCII characters per path (208,621 paths) give a 67,176,917-byte artifact on the branch (over the cap; the run is recorded and quarantined, the next snapshot refuses), 10 per path give 79,038,511 bytes; on origin/main the same 10-per-path input has its run row refused (ARIA-HIGH-617) and a 59,368,510-byte artifact. Deadline: HIGH, 12 days, with ARIA-HIGH-618. [canonicalize-owner 2026-10-19: owner_user okan -> Okan-wqm — ARIA-MEDIUM-535 owner identity is the CODEOWNERS handle]

Main fixed that row's failure scenario in 577741a4d: the perimeter now binds from the latest row carrying a change_id, so the merge lane's own observed row (GitHub's payload, change_id None) no longer unbinds every ARIA PR. The writer and the readers stayed as they were. Measured on origin/main a488a36f2 by the ARIA order chain with the wave-3 G003-md1-binding bucket's tests (chain/items/G003-md1-binding/red.log): an observed row whose payload names chg_forged is written with chg_forged, and change_for_pr then returns chg_forged instead of the opener's change; a legacy observed row carrying a change_id binds the PR; record_pr_lifecycle accepts a missing event and the unknown event pr_open; _reverted_suite stages the suite of a later row's proposal; _merge_index returns the PR's merged row for an unrelated change named only by an observed row; the assessment capture accepts an observed row as the change's opening. Before it (d9d171193) an ls-tree miss below a symlinked directory was policy_invalid; 02e4c0dc6 reads it as an owed proof. Measured on origin/main 57afe1e15 by the ARIA order chain with the wave-3 G003-A19-1-AB bucket's tests (chain/items/G003-A19-1-AB/red.log): the pinned ref's parent directory committed as a symlink, Mode-A proven, gives ('live_proven', ('closure_policy_regression_refs_unresolved',)) where the policy is invalid; a git failure on that ancestor is never seen because no ancestor is read; an unpinned ref is ls-tree'd before the pinned comparison refuses it (the wave-3 security review measured up to 123 calls per such ref once an ancestor walk exists). Failure scenario: a target tree replaces aria-kernel/tests (or tools/aria-adapters) with a symlink; the status reports the operator's tampered tree as engineering backlog and, with Mode-A proven, readiness live_proven. Fix: one classification per pinned ref (landed: a regular blob; unlanded: absent and every existing ancestor a tree; irregular otherwise, an invalid policy; a git failure on the ref or an ancestor is invalid), and the pinned references are compared before any ref reaches git. title: Authority acts with no approval-vocabulary parameter escape the ARIA-HIGH-238 pin: `aria-kernel state lease release --force-foreign` releases another host's aria/state writer lease on a free --reason, with no operator act
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cli.py:731-742 (--force-foreign needs only a non-empty --reason; the release runs with token=None)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/state_writer_lease.py:763-766 (force_foreign_reason releases the lease whoever holds it; the holder's run liveness is only written into the reason, never a refusal)
aria-kernel/tests/test_operator_approval_callers.py:78 (the pin's population is parameter-name based, APPROVAL_PARAMETER, so a raise whose function has no such parameter is never classified)
rule_violated: Every operator approval is proven by the operator's own GitHub act (plan 037 operator decision 2), and the gate that enforces it must see every authority-widening act, not only the functions whose parameter is named like an approval reference.
notes: Residual 1 of the wave-3 G010-238-pin-breakers implementation (ARIA-HIGH-238 slices 1-2), named 'not covered' in wave2/design/G010.md; re-read by the ARIA order chain on origin/main e1f659819. Failure scenario: any process that can run the kernel CLI against the repository (an agent in the self-hosted lane included) runs `aria-kernel state lease release --force-foreign --reason x` and releases the writer lease a live holder on another host still uses; the next acquirer and the live holder then both act as the aria/state writer. Nothing asks for an operator act, and the ARIA-HIGH-238 pin cannot see it because release_writer_lease has no approval-reference parameter and calls no verifier. Fix direction: classify by authority effect (an inventory of the state writers that widen what ARIA may do), and prove a foreign release by an operator's GitHub act bound to the lease instance (lease_id, epoch), or refuse it while the holder's run is live. Deadline: registration + 90 days (MEDIUM ceiling).

title: A tool_unquarantine approval is scoped to the tool only, so an operator act posted for one quarantine of a tool also releases that tool's next quarantine within the act's max age
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/operator_approval.py:436-441 (the verifier bounds an act only by 'not in the future' and 'not older than approval_max_age_hours'; nothing ties it to the quarantine it answered)
rule_violated: An approval that clears a stop names the instance it clears (ARIA-HIGH-238: the breaker and MCP surfaces bind to tripped_at / quarantined_at), so an act posted for one stop cannot clear a later one.
notes: Residual 2 of the wave-3 G010-238-pin-breakers implementation, named 'not covered' in wave2/design/G010.md; re-read by the ARIA order chain on origin/main e1f659819. Failure scenario: the operator posts `surface=tool_unquarantine tool=X` for quarantine Q1 and the release is done with another act (or the act is posted and left unspent); X is quarantined again for a new reason (Q2); the unspent act, still inside approval_max_age_hours, releases Q2 although the operator never saw it. The breaker and MCP surfaces landed with ARIA-HIGH-238 slices 1-2 bind to the instance (tripped_at / quarantined_at through operator_approval.recorded_instance); tool_unquarantine does not. Fix direction: add the quarantine instance (the QUARANTINED transition's recorded_at) to the surface's scope, read by a tool_registry scope function, and print it from the CLI's --print-approval-line. Deadline: registration + 90 days (MEDIUM ceiling).

title: A breaker stop with no recorded trip binds to the constant scope value `none`, so an unspent tripped_at=none act pre-authorizes clearing a later unrecorded trip, including a failure-breaker reset while nothing is tripped
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/operator_approval.py:97-104 (NO_RECORDED_INSTANCE = "none"; recorded_instance maps an absent stamp to it)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:502-524 (trip_scope binds to `none` when the state file records no tripped_at)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:557-560 (reset writes {"state": "ok"} without tripped_at and truncates the ledger; reset_breaker has no not-tripped no-op)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:326 (evaluate_breaker can trip from damaged ledger rows alone, which writes no state, so the scope repeats as `none`)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cost_budget.py:281-288 (the same fallback in cost_budget.trip_scope, reachable only with a hand-edited state)
rule_violated: An approval that clears a stop names the instance it clears, so an act posted for one stop cannot clear a later one (ARIA-HIGH-238).
notes: Residual 3 of the wave-3 G010-238-pin-breakers implementation, with the scenario its fix round added (fix.md item 3); re-read by the ARIA order chain on the landing branch from origin/main e1f659819. Failure scenarios: (1) an operator act posted for a reset while the breaker is ok (scope tripped_at=none) and left unspent authorizes, within approval_max_age_hours, a reset that truncates a window still accumulating failures; (2) after a reset (state {state: ok}, no tripped_at), a later trip derived only from damaged ledger rows records no stamp, so an earlier unspent `none` act clears it. The documented exception is stated in operator_approval.py's AUTHORITY_RAISING_SURFACES comment. Fix direction: make it impossible: every trip writes its instance (evaluate_breaker's damaged-evidence verdict included), and reset_breaker is a no-op without an act when nothing is tripped, like cost_budget.reset_breaker. Deadline: registration + 180 days (LOW ceiling).

title: Breaker reset and evidence quarantine read the trip scope, verify the act over the network, then rewrite failures.jsonl without the ledger lock, so a failure recorded in between is cut without the act having seen it
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:527-570 (reset_breaker: trip_scope -> verify_operator_approval (GitHub API) -> atomic_write_json {state: ok} + failures_path.write_text(''), no lock held)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:384-460 (record_failure appends under append_jsonl's lock at :420 and rewrites tripped_at at :445)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:577-720 (quarantine_breaker_evidence reads, verifies, then rewrites the ledger the same way)
rule_violated: A write that clears a stop is atomic with the evidence the operator's act was bound to: the instance read for the scope and the ledger the write cuts are the same, under one lock.
notes: Residual 4 of the wave-3 G010-238-pin-breakers implementation; re-read by the ARIA order chain on the landing branch from origin/main e1f659819. Pre-existing truncate race that now also defeats the trip binding ARIA-HIGH-238 slices 1-2 added. Failure scenario: reset_breaker reads tripped_at=T1 and asks GitHub for the act (seconds); meanwhile record_failure appends F and restamps tripped_at=T2; the reset then writes {state: ok} and truncates failures.jsonl, cutting F, which the operator's act (bound to T1) never covered. Fix direction: take the ledger's lock around read-scope -> write (verification may stay outside if the scope is re-read and compared under the lock before the write). Deadline: registration + 180 days (LOW ceiling).

title: An undecodable cost-breaker state file reads as ok, so truncating a tripped breaker's state clears the cost stop with no operator act
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cost_budget.py:89-95 (_read_json returns the default {"state": "ok"} on JSONDecodeError or OSError)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cost_budget.py:122-127 (current_state answers ok for a state file it cannot decode; auto_action_gate reads it to gate the autonomous path)
rule_violated: Unreadable stop evidence means stopped (fail closed), as the failure breaker decides it since ORPHAN-CRITICAL-418; a stop clears only through its owner's verb, which now asks for the operator's act (ARIA-HIGH-238).
notes: Found by the wave-3 G010-238-pin-breakers fix round (fix.md, new-finding candidate, pre-existing); re-measured by the ARIA order chain on the landing branch from origin/main e1f659819 with chain/items/G010-238-pin-breakers/probe_cost_truncated.py: after cost_budget._trip_breaker current_state is 'tripped'; after truncating budget/breaker state to 20 bytes it is 'ok'. Failure scenario: a torn write, a disk-full truncation or any process that can write the tools store leaves the cost-state file undecodable; the cost stop ARIA-HIGH-238 now clears only on an operator's GitHub act reads as ok and the autonomous path spends past its cap. Fix direction: make it impossible: an unreadable or undecodable cost state is 'tripped' (a distinct unreadable reason), as circuit_breaker.current_state does for its ledger. Deadline: registration + 90 days (MEDIUM ceiling).

title: The ARIA-HIGH-238 pin's P5 checks the governance row that records a breaker reset, not the writes that clear the breaker, so a new writer that clears a stop without writing that row passes
evidence: aria-kernel/tests/test_operator_approval_callers.py:230 (RAISING_GOVERNANCE_KINDS: P5 pins the event kinds written only inside RAISING functions)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:557-560 (the clearing writes: atomic_write_json {state: ok} and the failures.jsonl truncation)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cost_budget.py:324 (the cost stop's clearing write: atomic_write_json {state: ok})
rule_violated: Make it detectable at the write: a stop is cleared only inside a function that verifies the operator's act, and a build-time gate fails any other writer of the cleared state.
notes: Rejected as out of the bucket's plan by the wave-3 G010-238-pin-breakers fix round (fix.md 'Rejected', LOW new-finding candidate); re-read by the ARIA order chain on the landing branch from origin/main e1f659819. Failure scenario: a later change adds a helper that writes {"state": "ok"} to the breaker state file (or truncates failures.jsonl) without appending circuit_breaker_reset; P5 sees no raising kind written outside a RAISING function and stays green, so the stop clears with no act. Fix direction: an AST detector of the clearing writes (the state-path call with an ok literal, the ledger truncation) plus a declared set of narrowing writers (record_failure, _trip_breaker), each write allowed only in a RAISING function. Deadline: registration + 180 days (LOW ceiling).

title: A breaker act binds to tripped_at in the rewritable state record, which can lag the failure ledger (a crash between record_failure's append and its restamp), so an unspent act for the older stamp clears failures the operator never saw
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:502-524 (trip_scope reads tripped_at from autonomous-state.json, not from the ledger)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:441-445 (and restamps tripped_at only afterwards, in a separate atomic_write_json; a kill between the two leaves the new row under the old stamp)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:336-337 (evaluate_breaker re-derives from the ledger precisely because the state record can desynchronise)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/circuit_breaker.py:557 (reset_breaker then truncates the whole window, the unseen row included)
rule_violated: An approval that clears a stop names the instance it clears, so evidence that arrives after the act was posted asks for a new act (ARIA-HIGH-238).
notes: Raised by the independent verification of the ARIA order chain item G010-238-pin-breakers (round 1, security lens) on the landing branch from origin/main e1f659819. The stale-stamp half of the instance binding; ARIA-LOW-666 is the `none` half and ARIA-LOW-667 the unlocked truncate, and the three share one fix. Failure scenario: the breaker trips at T1 (tripped_at=T1); the operator posts the approval line for T1 and does not present it yet; a further failure row is appended and the process is killed before atomic_write_json restamps the state (the reviewer also names a lost publish race or a continuity-gap recovery that adopts a remote state file still showing T1, state_store.rebase_store_onto_remote); trip_scope still returns T1, so the unspent T1 act (valid for approval_max_age_hours) passes and reset_breaker truncates a window holding a failure the act never covered. The evidence quarantine verb binds to the same scope. Needs a crash or an adopted remote state, and still an operator act for that breaker, so LOW. Fix direction (with ARIA-LOW-666/667): make it impossible: derive the instance from the evidence itself (the newest in-window failure row's ts, or a digest of the ledger), read under the ledger lock, and re-read and compare it under that lock before the write. Deadline: registration + 180 days (LOW ceiling).

title: ctutils 0.4.2 in the root Cargo lockfile carries RUSTSEC-2026-0385 (non-constant-time mask generation and u128 comparisons, published 2026-10-23); the Audit root lockfile step of sens-api-gateway-rust fails and turns the required sens-enterprise-summary red on every PR that runs it
evidence: Cargo.lock:501-505 (ctutils 0.4.2 at origin/main d0daf0032; only dependent digest 0.11.2, under hmac 0.13.0, md-5 and sha2 of postgres-protocol 0.6.12, reached by sensor-ingestion and outbox-rs through tokio-postgres and deadpool-postgres, and by router-coprocessor through hmac and sha2)
.github/workflows/ci-affected.yml:1582-1583 (Audit root lockfile, cargo audit --deny warnings; failed in CI run 39923595892 on RUSTSEC-2026-0385)
.github/workflows/rust-ci.yml:223-228 (the root cargo audit of the Rust CI workflow; its ignore list does not cover RUSTSEC-2026-0385)
rule_violated: No unreviewed advisory in any audited Rust lockfile: an advisory with a patched in-range release is fixed by upgrading the lockfile, never by an audit ignore
notes: External drift: RustSec published RUSTSEC-2026-0385 on 2026-10-23 against an unchanged lockfile. The only secret-dependent ctutils comparison reached is the SCRAM client's ServerSignature check (postgres-protocol sasl.rs:300, hmac.verify_slice); only the Postgres server or a TLS-terminating attacker can time it, the value is bound to one handshake and the client aborts on the first mismatch, and no 32-bit target is built, hence LOW. Fix: cargo update -p ctutils --precise 0.4.4 in the root workspace (first patched release, rust-version 1.87, within the 1.88.0 toolchain); the other four audited lockfiles hold no ctutils.

title: tokio 1.52.1 in the sens-api-gateway and gateway-fuzz Cargo lockfiles carries RUSTSEC-2026-0386 (AsyncFd::new and related safe constructors violate I/O safety, published 2026-10-13); the Audit gateway lockfile step of sens-api-gateway-rust fails and turns the required sens-enterprise-summary red on every PR that runs it
evidence: sens-api-gateway/Cargo.lock:4180-4183 (tokio 1.52.1 at origin/main ddf6d5723; patched releases are >= 1.51.6 < 1.52.0 and >= 1.53.3, so the 1.52 line has no fix)
.github/workflows/ci-affected.yml:1584-1592 (Audit gateway lockfile, cargo audit --deny warnings; RUSTSEC-2026-0386 is not in its ignore list, so the unsound warning fails the step)
.github/workflows/sens-api-gateway-ci.yml:345-352 (the same gateway audit in the gateway CI workflow)
.github/workflows/edge-agent-release.yml:222-227 (the same gateway audit gates the edge agent release)
sens-api-gateway/src/modbus.rs:845-853 (Modbus RTU through rodbus spawn_rtu_client_task, which opens the serial port through tokio-serial 5.4.5, the only AsyncFd caller in the gateway graph)
rule_violated: No unreviewed advisory in any audited Rust lockfile: an advisory with a patched in-range release is fixed by upgrading the lockfile, never by an audit ignore
notes: External drift: RustSec published RUSTSEC-2026-0386 (informational = unsound, memory-corruption; tokio-rs/tokio#8587) against an unchanged lockfile. The affected functions are tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::{new, with_interest, try_new, try_with_interest}. Neither suderra-agent nor the vendored crates call them; the only caller in the gateway graph is tokio-serial 5.4.5 (SerialStream::open, pair, TryFrom<TTYPort>), and it wraps a mio-serial SerialStream that owns its file descriptor for the AsyncFd's lifetime. The use-after-free needs the registered descriptor to be duplicated and closed while the AsyncFd lives, which no safe or unsafe code in suderra-agent does (its only libc::close calls are on its own memfd_secret descriptors, never registered with tokio). Unsound API present, no reachable misuse, hence LOW. The root lockfile is already on tokio 1.54.1 (patched). Fix: tokio 1.52.1 -> 1.53.3 (first patched release above the 1.52 line, rust-version 1.71, identical dependency requirements) in sens-api-gateway/Cargo.lock and sens-api-gateway/fuzz/Cargo.lock; version and checksum only.
